description: The Hartekind Run and Social Run is being organized for the third time by Rotary Club Voorburg-Vliet in collaboration with Sparta Voorburg Athletics Club. The event offers several distances: 1 km and 2.5 km junior runs, an 800-meter Social Run, and 5 km and 10 km adult runs. The start is on the athletics track at Sparta Voorburg, and the course runs along Westvlietweg, Schrepelpad, the cycle bridge, the ADO stadium, and cycle tunnels. All proceeds are donated to Stichting Hartekind, giving the event a social and sporting character.
course_highlights: Start and finish on the athletics track at Sparta Voorburg
Course along Westvlietweg, Schrepelpad, the cycle bridge, the ADO stadium, and cycle tunnels
10 km participants run two laps; 5 km participants run one lap
additional: The Social Run consists of two 400-meter laps on the athletics track. The 2.5 km junior run starts at 10:15, the Social Run at 10:00, and the adult runs (5 km and 10 km) at 10:45. All event proceeds go to Stichting Hartekind. The exact course and distances are not specified; the event focuses on social and inclusive participation.

name: 24. Röntgenlauf
description: The Röntgenlauf in Remscheid is a traditional cross-country race with various distances, including 5 km, 10 km, half marathon, marathon and ultramarathon. The half marathon is especially popular, attracting up to 1,500 participants, and is considered one of Germany’s largest cross-country races. The routes pass through varied natural scenery, with forest trails and paved sections; the half marathon covers about one third of the Röntgenweg. A shuttle service takes half marathon participants from the finish back to the start. The event also places emphasis on environmental protection by recommending reusable drinking cups.
course_highlights: 5 km and 10 km races on a loop between Hackenberg and Wuppersperre, with approximately 95 m and 190 m of elevation gain, respectively
Half marathon with approximately 405 m of ascent and 560 m of descent; part of the ultramarathon route
Route along forest trails and paved sections; not suitable for spiked shoes
additional: The half marathon has a minimum age of 16; the marathon and ultramarathon have a minimum age of 18. Minors need written consent from a parent or guardian. There is a clothing transport service from the start to the finish and a bus transfer from the finish back to the start. Participants are asked to bring their own reusable drinking cups to help protect the environment. The entry fee includes a race bib, finisher’s medal and refreshments. Distances range from 5 km to the ultramarathon (63.3 km), including children’s races and cross-country races; registration is open until 25 October 2026.

name: Heemstedeloop
location: Sportparklaan and Landgoed Groenendaal, Heemstede, North Holland, Netherlands
description: The Heemstede Loop takes place on 25 October 2026 in Heemstede and offers an atmospheric running experience through the beautiful Groenendaalse Bos and lively Heemstede. Participants are cheered on by enthusiastic spectators and entertained along the way by live music from bands and DJs, creating a festive atmosphere. Several distances are available, including a 1 km FamilyRun for children, a 5 km, and a 10 km route that covers the 5 km loop twice. Organiser SportSupport Kennemerland ensures a well-organised and enjoyable event, with timing and unique medals for all participants.
course_highlights: Route through the beautiful Groenendaalse Bos and lively Heemstede
The 10 km route consists of two laps of the 5 km loop
Live music from bands and DJs along the course
additional: The Les Petits 1 km FamilyRun is suitable for children aged 4 and up, with two start groups: groups 1–4 start at 10:00 and groups 5–8 at 10:30. One parent or guardian may run for free with children in groups 1–4. Timing is provided by Chronorace. Registration includes a unique medal, refreshments along the route and after the finish, and changing facilities. Registration is via a digital module. Race numbers are sent by post or handed out on the day. Facilities include changing and shower rooms and a supervised cloakroom.

name: 26. Dresden-Marathon / DRESDEN-MARATHON
description: The DRESDEN-MARATHON has been held regularly in late October since 1999. It offers a flat, fast course through the Saxon state capital, passing its famous sights. The route goes through the historic Old Town, including Brühl’s Terrace, the Semper Opera House and other Baroque buildings, as well as the lively Neustadt district. More than 300 musicians and numerous bands create a special atmosphere along the course. The second half of the marathon runs through the Blasewitz district, with views of the palaces on the Loschwitz Elbe slope and the villas along Goetheallee, before returning to the Old Town along the Elbe.
course_highlights: Flat, fast course through Dresden’s historic Old Town and Neustadt district
Illuminated Waldschlößchen Tunnel and bridge, and the Großer Garten
Atmosphere created by more than 300 musicians and bands along the course
additional: More than 300 musicians and numerous bands create an atmosphere along the course. There is a marathon expo, race-pack collection and a SPARKASSEN pacemaker service. After the race, medal engraving, a photo service, showers, changing rooms and toilets, as well as award ceremonies, are available. The evening before the race, an anniversary party takes place in the marquee behind Heinz Steyer Stadium (€25 admission; limited capacity). Several race distances, online registration, health questionnaire, event on 24 and 25 October 2026

name: Oeventroper Volks- und Straßenlauf
location: Sportplatz 'In den Oeren', Arnsberg-Oeventrop, Arnsberg, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany
description: The Oeventrop Volks- und Straßenlauf is a local road race in Arnsberg-Oeventrop, held at the “In den Oeren” sports ground. The main event is a flat 10 km race for adults, which starts in the morning. There is also a 5 km youth race and several 1.1 km children’s races, divided by age and gender. The start and finish are centrally located at the sports ground, making the event family-friendly and easy to navigate. The event is hosted by TuS 1896 Oeventrop e.V. and is part of the Lauf Cup standings.
course_highlights: Flat 10 km circuit
5 km youth race on a flat loop
1.1 km children’s races divided by age and gender
additional: The start and finish are at the “In den Oeren” sports ground, bringing everything together in one place for runners and families. There is a three-person team classification for the 5 km race. The children’s races have separate starts for different age and gender groups. Race in Arnsberg-Oeventrop, Lauf Cup standings, parking at REWE and ALDI Widayweg

name: Halloween-Run-Bremen
description: The Halloween Run Bremen 2026 takes place on October 31 and offers runners a spooky race experience around Werdersee. With five different distances, from 1 km to the 42.195 km marathon, there is something for every ability level. The courses are measured in accordance with German Athletics Association rules and are eligible for record lists, underscoring the competitive nature of the event. Alongside the sporting event, participants can look forward to a spooky atmosphere with costumes, lights and fog, as well as an awards ceremony and a closing fireworks display.
course_highlights: 8.333 km loop course, measured by the German Athletics Association and eligible for record lists
Distances from 1 km (Spuklauf) to the marathon (Splatterthon), with a spooky atmosphere
Start and finish area at Werdersee, between the Finnbahn and the barbecue area
additional: The awards ceremony for the Spuklauf takes place immediately after the finish; awards for the other distances are presented later. A spectacular fireworks display at 18:00 rounds off the event. There are also relay competitions for the marathon (5-person relay). The race bib with RFID chip serves as the relay baton and must be brought by the team. Costumes are expressly encouraged but are not compulsory. Participants can register online. There are various distances and relay options; the event takes place at night and offers a spooky atmosphere.

name: Guldfeber Aarhus — Golden Fever #1
description:
Gold Fever — Denmark’s first SplitRace tournament. A free running game in the streets of Aarhus: 12 segments (0.4–1.9 km) are mapped around the city, and 7 of them form a hidden “golden chain” — nobody knows which ones, or in what order. Find them. Run them. Chase the times.

No mass start and no entry fee: run whenever you want, as often as you want, throughout 17 October – 1 November. The app measures your times via GPS. You earn points for each golden segment based on how close you are to the fastest time — women are scored against the fastest woman, men against the fastest man. Extra points go to the first runners to unlock a golden segment — and the tournament’s biggest bonus goes to the first to complete the whole chain in the correct order.

This is the first edition — a pilot for a maximum of 30 runners. Your feedback will shape the game.

(EN: A free city-wide running game in Aarhus. 12 segments, 7 of them secretly form a golden chain — find them and beat the clock. No mass start: run anytime 17 Oct – 1 Nov. Free entry, GPS timing in the SplitRace app. First edition, 30 pilot spots.)
additional: No start line and no start groups — all segments are on public, lit routes around Aarhus, and you can run them whenever you want during the event window. Participation requires the free SplitRace app (iOS / Android) — download it via splitrace.app, join the “Guldfeber Aarhus” tournament, and all 12 segments will appear on your map. Limited to the first 30 runners. Open streets: follow normal traffic rules. Questions? Write to support@splitrace.app or Instagram https://www.instagram.com/split_race/

description: Höstmilen is a trail race in the Kolmården forests outside Åby, north of Norrköping, taking place on 1 November 2026. The course follows trails between Sörsjön and Lillsjön and offers scenic, challenging terrain for both competitive runners and recreational participants. The event is organised by OK Kolmården and has three main race options: the classic 10.6 km, Höstfemman 5.2 km, and races for children and young people.

name: Kullamannen by UTMB
description: Set along the rocky shores of Sweden's Kullaberg, Kullamannen by UTMB® offers trail courses that range from a fast 20 km to a challenging 100-mile test of endurance. Runners traverse rocky headlands, beech and pine forests, and coastal paths with dramatic ocean views, making it an adventure-focused event for trail runners of varying ambitions. The event weekend combines technical coastal terrain, well-supported aid stations and organised race services to welcome both international and local participants.
course_highlights: Rocky coastal trails and cliffs along Kullaberg with ocean views
Runs through beechwood and pine forest singletrack and compact dirt trails
North Shore 20K features narrow beachside paths and a night start (headlamp required)
additional: Minimum ages: North Shore open to runners born in 2010 or before. Registration sales windows: UTMB Index holders 18 - 20 Nov 2025 (exclusive), open to all from 20 Nov 2025 until 10 Oct 2026 or until sold out. Registration includes race bib, access to aid stations, baggage transport depending on distance, medical assistance and after-race services. Transfer to a shorter distance allowed until 3 weeks before the event (deadline: 2026-10-10). Bib distribution and expo in Båstad on the event weekend. Races range from 22 km to 100 miles; start in Höganäs, via Mölle and Kullaberg, finish in Båstad; November weather can be tough; DNF rate 40-60% for 100-milers; Running Stone lottery and direct qualification for the UTMB World Series Finals.

description: Finalloppet is western Sweden’s largest cross-country race. It has been organised by Göteborgs Skidklubb since 1968 and is held at Skatås Motionscentrum in Gothenburg. The event offers several distances (19 km, 10 km, 5.3 km, 2.3 km and 1.9 km, as well as Paraloppet and Parvelbanan) for both competitive and recreational runners. The courses alternate between technical trail sections and wider forest roads, and are marked with clear arrows and kilometre markers. The organiser brings the finish area and services together at the event venue at Skatås and provides water stations, medical care and a sweep crew on all courses.
course_highlights: The 19 km course has an advanced trail section of approximately 2,500 metres
The 10 km course includes a trail section just over 500 metres long that is often wet, muddy and rocky

additional: Registration is handled via RaceID (payment by card, Swish or Google Pay and Mobile BankID). You can register several people at the same time and buy gift cards via RaceID. The organiser offers Startklar insurance as an optional add-on, which reimburses the entry fee in the event of illness, injury or pregnancy. The event venue is at Skatås Motionscentrum, with finish and service tents, a medical tent at the finish, and medical staff at certain water stations (Ugglemossen and Svarttjärn). The sweep crew sets off after the last start for each course and is responsible for runners still on the course. Donate 50 kronor to Jontefonden when registering; a GPX file is available to download for the 19 km course.

It takes place amid the beautiful natural surroundings of Christinehof Castle in Andrarum, Skåne County, and has 500 metres of elevation gain.

name: Billingen Trail
description:
We invite you to enjoy running on Billingen. This year, the start and finish will be at the Stadium in the Billingen Recreation Area.
The long course is just over 47 km with approximately 930 metres of elevation gain. It goes all the way around northern Billingen, along beautiful trails by the edge of the mountain. As a runner, you’ll experience varied terrain, including deciduous forest, mountain ravines, meadows and spruce forest, as well as beautiful views across the landscape from several places. The surface varies from easy-to-run sections and approximately 6 km of asphalt to some more challenging parts.

The middle-distance course, 21 km, follows the northern section of the Billinge Trail and has approximately 500 metres of elevation gain. The course includes a mix of trails, meadows and roads.

Our shortest distance, 12 km, has just over 200 metres of elevation gain and follows trails of varying difficulty, with some short sections on roads.

Information about the courses and markings may change.

Start:

47 km, 10:00, Stadium, Billingen Recreation Area, Skövde.
21 km, 10:45, Björnasäter, Lerdala. Bus departs from the Billingen Recreation Area at 10:05.
12 km, 11:30, Stadium, Billingen Recreation Area, Skövde.

Finish:

At the Stadium, Billingen Recreation Area, Skövde.

All finishers cross the finish line at the stadium.

name: Isaberg500
description:
Isaberg 500 is the race we love running ourselves and the foundation of the entire trail weekend. It’s a perfect mix of trails, hills, sweat and tears that brings to mind spectacular races in both the Swedish mountains and the Alps. Isaberg 500 also features switchbacks, long, enjoyable downhill stretches and fantastic views. In between, you can enjoy winding trails through enchanting forests. Isaberg 500 includes at least 500 metres of elevation gain and is perfect for anyone training for a mountain marathon or similar race.

NEW FOR 2025!
When Isaberg500 started, Jättestigen was a big talking point. A few years later, it was closed due to the risk of landslides. In 2025, Jättestigen returns as part of Isaberg500, but under a new name — Jättetrappan...

Isaberg500 is a race in the Outnorth Trail Tour 2025.
course_highlights: Trail race with varied trails and hills, with a technical character reminiscent of races in the mountains and the Alps
Multisport around the Isaberg summit: kayaking, mountain biking and trail running — Solo and Duo categories
Isaberg Gravel: a circuit of approximately 45 km, starting and finishing in Åsenhöga; Elite/up to age 50: 3 laps, older riders/sport recreation: 2 laps, recreational: 1 lap
additional: Contact GI by mobile at +46 703 815 118 or email at gimulti@gmail.com. Organisers: GI Folkestad and Martin Jepson. Guided rides for cycling groups can be booked; the organisers have ready-made routes that can be adapted to the group’s needs. Main distance: approximately 10.5 km (Distans Trailtour); Kids Trail: approximately 2 km with approximately 150 metres of elevation gain; start time: Sunday at 12:00; location: Isaberg/Anderstorp; contact: niklas@isabergtrail.se.

name: Kullamannen 100 miles
description: Kullamannen 100 miles is an extremely challenging A+ 100-mile race that takes you through 15 scenic nature reserves and two mountains in Skåne. The race starts in Höganäs with a prologue to Mölle and the mythical Kullaberg, where you’ll encounter technical singletrack in one of Sweden’s most popular nature reserves. After 66 kilometres, runners can refuel with hot soup before continuing north towards Ängelholm and Torekov, with the finish in Båstad. With a DNF rate of 40–60%, the race is a major challenge even for experienced runners.
course_highlights: Passes through 15 nature reserves and over two mountains
Technical singletrack in the Kullaberg nature reserve
Starts in Höganäs and finishes in Båstad, with an opportunity to refuel after 66 km
additional: The race starts in Höganäs, with buses departing from Båstad. Race bibs can be collected at the Expo in Båstad with valid ID and a QR code. Drop bags are handed out at bib collection and are available at the Båstad Aid Station and after the finish. Drop bags must be collected within two hours of the race ending. Late registration and transfers to a shorter distance are possible until 10 October 2026. The awards ceremony takes place in Båstad on the Saturday after the race. Race bibs must be collected in person at the EXPO in Båstad with valid ID and a QR code. Some sections of the course cross private land and protected natural areas; access outside race day is not permitted.

name: Walking Dead Ultra 100 Miles
description: Walking Dead Ultra 100 miles is a challenging ultramarathon on a 32 km loop in Paradiset Nature Reserve in Huddinge. Participants can choose from three distances: 100 miles (5 laps), 100 km (3 laps plus an extra course) and 65 km (2 laps). The course follows the Sörmlandsleden trail for most of the way and offers a mix of forest trails and roads. All categories start at the same time, and the race has a 36-hour time limit. Drop bags, a toilet, and access to water, tea, coffee and broth are available to participants at Torpet Paradiset.
course_highlights: The course mostly follows the Sörmlandsleden trail
Each lap is approximately 32 km long
The race takes place in Paradiset Nature Reserve on forest trails and roads
additional: All categories start at the same time, with a maximum time limit of 36 hours. Drop bags can be left at Torpet Paradiset, where there is access to a dry toilet, cold and hot water, tea, coffee and broth. Parking is available, but carpooling is encouraged because space is limited. The start area can be reached by bus or car. At the lap point, water, coffee, tea, broth and a dry toilet are available. Bus 709 runs from Huddinge station to Bruket or Ådran; parking is available, but spaces are limited.

name: Backyard Ulötra Sölvesborg
description:
What is Backyard Ultra?
Backyard Ultra takes place on a marked 6,706-metre loop, and each participant has one hour to complete it. A new start takes place at the top of every hour, and as long as you can complete the loop within an hour, you remain in the race. You win by being the most enduring and ultimately getting to run one final lap alone! A fun race and concept with a very welcoming, community-minded atmosphere, where many participants set their distance records!

Some sections take you past cultural sites, as much of the route passes through the historic cultural heritage of Finnskogen. Enjoy a memorable trail-running experience with plenty of challenging climbs and, in some places, technical trails. Welcome to a true adventure!

description:
Welcome to HIIT OUT – Trailrun – a trail race with challenging running and a wonderful experience in nature!

name: Ultra Caballo Blanco Suecia
description:
Only the 100-mile race starts on Friday (08:00); the 100 km and 50-mile races start on Saturday (06:00).
All three races have their own routes (they have nothing in common with CBMR, which takes place on the same day). The 50-mile and 100-mile races have some staffed aid stations, which are also shared with the 100 km race, which has its own stations as well. The 100-mile race is virtually entirely unsupported, apart from a few unmanned water stations. You also pass a well-stocked country store and a church with water and toilets.
All three races offer the option of a drop bag.
The courses are completely unmarked, so you navigate using a downloaded GPX file...
additional:
We don’t have paper cups, so bring a cup!
Hot food, drinks, coffee and cake are served after the finish.

The entry fee includes 120:-, which is sent to a children’s race in Urique, Mexico!

name: Caballo Blanco Memorial Run (CBMR)
description:
This is the route that Caballo Blanco (aka Micah True) and I ran on 2011-09-26, when he was visiting Sweden at my invitation. In spring 2012, we received the news that he had died. We then organised a memorial race on 2012-09-22. It became a tradition, and eventually the race offered 1, 2 or 4 laps of the route, which is approximately 11 km and has approximately 150 metres of elevation gain.
See also Ultra Caballo Blanco Suecia — an ultra race held at the same time.
An article I wrote quite a while ago, when we introduced the 50-mile race:
https://redsports.se/CBM/TheStory.html
additional:
The 4-lap race starts at 12:00, while the 1- and 2-lap races start at 15:00.
Please note that you must bring your own cup/mug.
The entry fee includes drinks, energy products, and a hot meal with coffee and cake after the race.

name: Löparfesten
description:
The running festival offers several different races, with something for everyone!

Whether you’re looking to set a personal best in the half marathon or prefer a walk with good friends, there’s a great race to choose from!

EKO ½Maran is for experienced runners, FORMTOPPEN Milen is a wonderful challenge, and the slightly shorter Here We Go 5an is for happy recreational runners or those who prefer to run fast but short. For those who want to take it a little easier, perhaps bring walking poles or a stroller, or simply enjoy nature, there’s Here We Go 5an – Promenad!

name: Änglamilen
description: Änglamilen is a long-established fun run in the heart of Ängelholm. Participants experience the town, the sea and the forest all in the same 10 kilometres. The 5 km race begins with a lovely run through the park in the charming Hembygdsparken. After approximately 2.7 km, the course crosses the Rönne River and continues along the beautiful riverside path in Nybroskogen. Finally, the course turns back across the river, with a sprint to the finish at Tullakrok. The 10 km course starts the same way as the 5 km route, but turns north after about a kilometre. Runners are treated to beautiful views over Skälderviken and its harbour, with Kullaberg visible in the background. After approximately 7.7 km, the courses join again, and runners can enjoy the beautiful riverside path in Nybroskogen.

The deadline for standard registration is 18 May, but late registration is available until one hour before the start of each race.

name: VABIK Terrengkarusell
description: VABIK Terrain Carousel 2025 will be held on Wednesdays and Thursdays, featuring marked trails and kilometer signs. The trails are marked from Wednesday at 1:00 PM to Thursday at 6:00 PM. On Wednesday, registration is from 3:00 PM to 6:00 PM, while on Thursday, registration begins at 1:00 PM. The mass start for the short course is at 5:30 PM, the Milsluker at 5:00 PM (not for all races), and the Children's Race at 5:10 PM (some races). All participants must collect a new race number from April 3rd.
course_highlights: The courses are marked from Wednesday at 1:00 PM to Thursday at 6:00 PM.
Mass start short course at 5:30 PM, Milsluker at 5:00 PM (not for all races), Children's race at 5:10 PM (some races).
Registration of completed/personal time on Wednesday from 3:00 PM to 6:00 PM.

name: Mobergslia Opp
description: Os Turn Athletics is organizing the uphill race Mobergslia Opp! The race features 2 different distances, and all participants will have their times recorded. Prizes will be awarded to the top three in each category, while all participants in the youth category will receive prizes. The event will take place at Kuvågen outdoor area/Mobergslia, with bib number distribution starting at 5:15 PM and prize distribution after the race.
course_highlights: Everyone gets their time recorded.
Prizes for the top three in each category.
In the recruit class, there are prizes for everyone!

name: Terrengkarusellen 1. løp
description: The Terrain Carousel 1st race starts at Fant Olsen and takes the participants down to Svarttjønn before they go up to the right by the parking lot. The route follows the outer road towards the 2nd stamping area, over the dam, and further down towards the town, before it turns up towards the viewpoint and the direction of the Tele building. Participants will also pass the birch grove and up the stairs to the 4th stamping area, before they follow the lit trail and end up on the path through the heather, which leads down towards the finish line. Have a great trip!
course_highlights: The course starts at Fant Olsen and goes down to Svarttjønn.
The participants follow the outer path towards the 2nd water station and over the dam.
The course includes a stretch through the birch grove and up the stairs to 4. Stampe.

name: Valestrandsmarka Rundt 1. løp
description: Valestrandsmarka Rundt Race 1 is a popular trail run taking place on April 11, 2025, starting at 6:45 PM and organized by Osterøy I.L. The race offers a varied and scenic course in Valestrandsmarka, where participants can look forward to challenging climbs and beautiful descents. This recreational run has previously attracted many participants and is known for its stunning surroundings and exciting challenges.
course_highlights: The course takes participants through scenic areas and offers varied challenges.
Valestrandsmarka Rundt was held in 2014 with 75 participants, and there have been several impressive performances over the years.
The next race is scheduled for April 25th.

name: Mortenløpene Terrengløp
description: Gjesdal Sports Club invites you to the Morten Races 2024, featuring the District Championship in Cross-Country Running. The race will take place on April 6th at 1:00 PM in Njåskogen, Bryne. The schedule will be published approximately one week before the race, with the youngest participants starting at 1:00 PM, while the 5-10 km distances will start at 2:30 PM. The Morten Races is a wonderful trail run on soft paths that offers races for all ages and levels, with distances ranging from a children's race of 325 meters to a long cross-country race of 10 kilometers.
course_highlights: The Morten Races are a great trail run on soft paths that have races for all ages and levels.
Distances range from children's races at 325 meters to cross-country races with a long course of 10 kilometers.
The trails are well-prepared and cleared, thanks to the efforts of the passionate Morten Karlsen and Gjesdal IL.

images.alt_text: Runner in the forest during the Morten races.

name: Bakgårdsultra Høyanger
description: Høyanger Backyard Ultra is a "backyard ultra" concept where you compete against the clock and yourself. In classic ultrarunning style, there will be laps starting every full hour, with each lap being 6.5 km and a maximum of 10 laps. This is a race for everyone – whether you want to chase kilometers and battle for first place, or if you just want to try one or two laps. How many laps you want to run is up to you – the most important thing is to show up!
course_highlights: Each lap is 6.5 km, and there is a maximum of 10 laps.
This is a race for everyone – whether you're looking to chase kilometers and battle for first place, or if you just want to try a lap or two.
How many laps you want to run is up to you – the most important thing is to show up!

name: Bergen Ultra Marathon
description: Bergen Ultra is part of the Marathon Carousel, which organizes long races in collaboration with BFG Bergen Running Club. This event includes both 63.3 km and 100 km distances, and the Norwegian Championship 100 km has been held six times. The Marathon Carousel focuses on the quality of the events and aims for all participants to enjoy themselves, despite the tough challenges.
course_highlights: The Marathon Carousel organizes Bergen Ultra with both 63.3 km and 100 km distances.
The NM 100 km has been organized six times by the Marathon Carousel.
The Marathon Carousel is focused on quality in its races and wants all participants to enjoy themselves.

name: Solsiå Sentrumsløp
description: This Saturday, it’s YOU who decides how far you want to run. The loop course is 3 kilometers long, and you can run as many laps as you wish within 6 hours. You can take breaks and stop the run whenever you like, but the breaks must be taken at the finish line (Langgata/Melkebaren). There will be a results list and awards for 3 km, 9 km, 21 km, and 42 km, as well as a special prize for the person who runs the most laps during the 6 hours and for the one with the most creative contribution.
course_highlights: The race has a duration of 6 hours, and you can take breaks whenever you wish.
There will be a results list/awards for 3 km, 9 km, 21 km, and 42 km.
Special prizes for the one who runs the most laps and for the one with the most creative contribution.

name: Drammen 10K
description: Drammen 10K is a running experience that takes you through a flat and fast course. The race starts at the corner of Drammenshallen and runs along the river, offering a beautiful view. Participants can expect a well-organized event with enthusiasm and support from the crowd. The course, known as one of Europe's fastest, has an elevation gain of 22 meters and provides a pleasant experience regardless of skill level.
course_highlights: The first 1000 meters are very fast and pancake flat.
Over 2000 runners were registered for the first edition, and both the Kenyan world elite and Norwegian runners set personal records.
The finish line is just outside Strømsø Center on Schwartz Street, where participants receive their medals after crossing the finish.

name: Vintarkarusell Eikanger 7
description: The second race in the winter series 2025-26 will be on Saturday, November 15, at Eikanger. In total, there will be seven races this season, three before Christmas and four after New Year. The course is the usual one around Eikangervågen, and registration starts from 2:20 PM.
course_highlights: The race is part of the winter series with a total of seven races this season.
There will be three races before Christmas and four after New Year.
Registration for the race starts at 2:20 PM.

images.alt_text: Map of terrain with a course, possibly for a race.

name: KRS Ultra
description: It is with great pleasure that we invite you to a fantastic running experience! Join us and explore the beautiful, urban terrain that Kristiansand has to offer. Whether you are an experienced runner with countless ultramarathons behind you, or you are a complete beginner curious about this exciting world, KRSUltra is the perfect way to kick off the season. KRSUltra 60 is a long race in the hills around Kristiansand, featuring a well-marked route that does not require a map or compass.
course_highlights: Participants will have access to drink and food stations along the way, as well as the option for drop bag transport.
A warm meal will be served at the finish line, and it is required to bring your own cup or bottle for drinks.
The maximum time for the race is 12 hours, and it is important to inform the organizer if you need to withdraw from the race.

name: Holmestrand Maraton
description: Holmestrand Marathon starts in the city center with a 5 km loop that goes through the northern and southern parts of the town. Participants can choose from several distances, including 5 km, 10 km, half marathon, full marathon, as well as ultrarunning and children's races. The course is fast with few inclines, and many runners will pass through the center several times, creating a lively atmosphere with enthusiastic cheering crowds. When you cross the finish line, a medal, honor, and glory await you, and no matter which distance you choose, you are a winner!
course_highlights: Holmestrand Marathon features a fast course with few uphill sections, ideal for both beginners and experienced runners.
There is a varied offering with distances ranging from a 200-meter kids' race to a marathon, as well as the Daily Double, which combines the marathon distance with a 10 km.
The race promotes public health and motivation, where participants support each other in reaching their goals.

name: KM Terrengløp Korte
description: We welcome you to the KM cross-country race short course at Ørin on April 13, 2024. Verdal Athletics Club is pleased to invite you to spring's most beautiful adventure at Ørin recreational area in Verdal. The course is known for its hilly terrain with elevation changes, providing an exciting challenge for the participants.
course_highlights: Welcome to the KM cross-country race short course at Ørin on April 13, 2024.
Verdal Athletics Club is pleased to invite you to the most beautiful adventure of spring.
The course is known for being hilly with elevation changes.

name: Drammen 10k
description: Experience an easy-to-run course ideal for both beginners and elite athletes. The Drammen 10k offers a flat and fast route that gives you the opportunity to perform your best, starting at the corner of Drammenshallen. The course winds through scenic areas in Drammen, and the first 1000 meters are very fast and pancake flat. The finish line is just outside Strømsø Senter on Schwartz Gate.
course_highlights: The flat course gives you the opportunity to perform your best.
The course takes participants through scenic areas in Drammen, with excellent conditions for running.
"The first 1000m is very fast and pancake flat."

name: Fredrikstadløpet
location: Bak Kongstenhallen, ved Gamlebyen i Fredrikstad
description: The Fredrikstad Race has international status and is for all categories of runners. It is a Quality Race with a certified course, and Kondis members receive a discount on the entry fee. The course crosses busy roads at certain points, and there are course marshals at all intersections to ensure the participants' safety.
course_highlights: The Fredrikstad Race is a Quality Race, which means that the course has been officially measured.
Kondis members receive a discount on the entry fee.
The course crosses a busy road at a couple of points, with course marshals at every intersection.

name: H3 Hamar Vårløp
description: Sunday, April 6th was a fantastic day along Lake Mjøsa with record participation in this year's H3 Hamar Hoka Spring Run. Many personal records were set in the sunshine under great running conditions, and the running season is officially underway. The Spring Run is open to everyone, and you can walk, jog, or run, with options of 5 or 10 km. We encourage everyone to stay in the area until all have crossed the finish line to cheer each other on!
course_highlights: WOW what a day! Finally a Spring Race with sunshine from a blue sky.
The fastest woman in the 10 km was Esther Innselseth with a time of 41:19.
We welcome everyone to participate, whether you want to walk, jog, or run.

name: Sørlandstesten 8
description: The Sørlandstest is a low-threshold recreational run for anyone looking for a positive running experience, regardless of ambition level. Whether you are training for a larger goal, want to feel the competition nerves, or just want a social and active day – this is the race for you! You can choose between 5 and 10 km, and all participants receive a medal and a high five. The event focuses on being inclusive and accommodating to all levels of runners, from beginners to experienced.
course_highlights: Choose between 5 and 10 km.
Medal and high five to everyone participating.
Flat and easy-to-run course.

name: Vinterkarusellen Løp 8
description: The Winter Carousel Race 8 is a certified running competition where times achieved in both 5 km and 10 km will be approved for statistics. Participants can earn a medal for a minimum of 5 completed races during the season. In 2023, there were 285 completed 5 km races and 159 completed 10 km races, with Andre Åsen (17:21) and Tonja Johansen (19:41) being the fastest in the 5 km, while Bjørn Seter Wastvedt (34:05) and Renate Galleberg (37:42) won the 10 km.
course_highlights: All times achieved in this year's Winter Carousel will be approved for statistics for both 5 and 10 km.
285 completed the 5 km while 159 reached the finish line in the double distance.
Andre Åsen (17:21) and Tonja Johansen (19:41) were the fastest in the 5 km, while Bjørn Seter Wastvedt (34:05) and Renate Galleberg (37:42) won the 10 km.

name: Sparebanken Sør Terrengkarusell
description: Welcome to the Sparebanken Sør Trail Carousel 2024! Everyone is welcome to the Trail Carousel – whether you want to walk, jog, or run. This year's season kicks off on Tuesday, April 9th at Dømmesmoen, with 16 races in varied terrain. The races take place on Tuesdays with a mass start at 6:00 PM (long) and 6:05 PM (short), along with a children's race at 5:30 PM. The week's course will be open and marked from Tuesday at 12:00 PM to Thursday at 7:30 PM.
course_highlights: The prizes in 2024 are beautiful glasses from Magnor Glassverk – of course delivered in a gift box.
You must participate in at least 10 of 16 races to be eligible for prizes.
We want more community spirit on Tuesdays, so we hope many will show up for the mass start.

name: Dogrun - Horten
description: Welcome to the season opener! In collaboration with Horten Flokkturer, we are once again organizing the VOM Dogrun in the beautiful Borreparken. Join us for a social and fun outing with your dog, alongside other dog lovers. You can choose to participate with or without timing, and every participant will receive a medal. Welcome to the whole family – both two-legged and four-legged!
course_highlights: Join a social and fun outing with your dog, in the company of other dog lovers.
You can choose with or without timing.
There is a participation medal for everyone.

name: Origo Solutions-løpet
description: Tuesday, August 19, the Origo Solutions Race at Hove is set to take place – the 10th race of the fall season. This race offers participants the chance to compete and enjoy a great atmosphere at Hove.
course_highlights: The Origo Solutions race is the 10th race of the fall season.
The race takes place at Hove.
The distance for the race is 4.4 km.

name: Vestfold Løpskarusell
description: Vestfold Running Carousel offers several distances for runners in beautiful surroundings, with races starting at 6:00 PM. Participants can choose between different laps and lengths, depending on which course they are participating in. Each course has its own character, with start and finish points near parking areas or well-known landmarks. Welcome to 8 fantastic races in the Tønsberg region, where everyone can participate, with or without timing.
course_highlights: All races start at 6:00 PM, and the timing will be electronic with results published via eqtiming.
Participants can choose to compete alone, with friends, family, or colleagues, and there are always several distances to choose from.
Come and experience the atmosphere, camaraderie, and joy of running together with a lot of wonderful people.

name: Skjalgstafetten
description: Welcome to the traditional Skjalg Relay, which is being held for the 53rd time this year in the Mosvann area. The relay is for children and young people aged 10 to 16, with participant prizes for the categories 10-12 years. The course is flat, and it is the same lap that is run a total of three times.
course_highlights: The relay is for children and young people between the ages of 10 and 16, with a participation prize in the 10-12 age categories.
The course is flat, and it is the same loop that is run a total of three times.
The EIK team participated for the first time in many years and finished third in their class, just one second behind the team that came in second.

name: Sandnes Ultratrail
description: In 2021, the adventure of Sandnes Ultratrail began. The race features distances of 100 miles, 50 miles, 43 km, 23 km, and 10 km, as well as a children's race. The trails wind through beautiful and varied nature, ranging from mountains with stunning fjord views to quiet forest paths, and there are opportunities for swimming in several lovely lakes along the routes. On the longest distance, participants traverse no less than 28 mountains and peaks, and all routes are technically challenging, adding an extra dimension to the experience.
course_highlights: The trails go through beautiful natural landscapes with a mix of technical terrain, forest, and gravel paths.
There are several aid stations along the routes, where experienced volunteers provide nourishment and care.
At the finish line, fantastic Jæder burgers, meat or vegan, are served straight from the grill, and we invite everyone to gather around the bonfire.

name: Tunnelløpet Bergen
description: The Tunnel Run Bergen is organized on a voluntary basis by BFG Bergen Running Club and Fyllingen Athletics. Any potential surplus is shared between the organizing clubs and will be fully used to promote sports activities under the two clubs' auspices – from children's and youth sports to recreational runners and athletes at a high national level. The race starts and finishes at Oasen Center in Fyllingsdalen, Bergen, and offers a distance of 5 km.
course_highlights: The Tunnel Run Bergen is organized by BFG Bergen Running Club and Fyllingen Athletics.
The proceeds from the race go towards promoting sports activities under the clubs' management.
The race starts and ends at Oasen Center, Fyllingsdalen, Bergen.

name: NM Terrengløp Stafett
description: We welcome you to the Norwegian Championships in cross-country running short course at Bjerkebanen, Oslo! The Norwegian Championships in cross-country relay, which takes place on Sunday, features teams consisting of two runners who each run three legs, alternating every time on 6 * 1 km. There are two different classes competing in the cross-country relay: Women Senior and Men Senior.
course_highlights: The teams consist of two runners who each run three legs.
The competition takes place at Bjerkebanen in Oslo.
There are competitions in two categories: Women's Senior and Men's Senior.

name: Perseløpet Maraton Vår
description: The Perseløpet Marathon Spring takes place on April 19 and includes various distances such as 5 km, 10 km, and Half Marathon. The course is fast and flat, designed for records, and is AIMS certified. Results are available immediately after finishing, and there is free parking for participants.
course_highlights: Fast and flat course, designed for records.
AIMS-certified course.
Results available immediately after finishing.

name: Oslo Løpsfestival
description: Oslo Running Festival consists of eight races along the capital's beautiful trails and scenic roads. You can run whenever you like – alone or together with others. You can participate individually in the SOLO category, or in the team competition as a DUO or TRIO, where you can compete in the women's, men's, and mixed classes. Each race is announced on Friday at 12:00, and the course is open until Sunday at 11:00 the following weekend, with a mass start precisely at 11:00.
course_highlights: You can run whenever you want – alone or together with others.
You can participate alone in the SOLO class, or in the team competition as a DUO or TRIO.
Each race is scheduled for an announced Friday at 12:00 PM.

name: Skjold på tvers
description: Skjold Across is a hiking event suitable for everyone, providing a fantastic nature experience in the village of Skjold. Participants meet at Skjold Arena for registration before being transported by bus to Hodnafjellet. Here, they walk through beautiful terrain with grand views via 9 peaks and back to the finish line at Skjold Arena, covering a distance of 23.8 km. There is also the option to walk half of the course, where participants are driven by bus to or from Dalavik, depending on where they choose to start.
course_highlights: You meet at Skjold Arena for registration, then the journey continues by bus to Hodnafjellet in the west.
You traverse beautiful terrain with grand views through 9 peaks and 23.8 km back to the finish line at Skjold Arena.
Buses run between 8:00 AM and 11:30 AM from Skjold Arena to Hodnafjellet.

name: Perseløpet #1
description: The Perseløpet is a low-threshold street race that offers a flat loop of just under 2.7 km, designed for records and AIMS-certified. Participants have the opportunity to test Synergy's so-called "Superfood Performance Beets" before the start, which is a concentrated beetroot drink. Results are available right after finishing, and there is free parking.
course_highlights: Fast and flat course, designed for records.
AIMS-certified course.
Participants will have the opportunity to test Synergy's so-called "Superfood Performance Beets" before the start.

name: Fjellhamarstafetten Ungdomsstafett
description: The Fjellhamarstafetten is a relay with eight stages that is very well suited for our long-distance runners, as several of the stages are hilly and allow them to leverage their running strength. Bøler's runners completed the relay in 26:54 minutes, which earned them a 4th place in the senior men's category. This has been the most important relay in terms of team selection for the Holmenkollstafetten, and several victories have been achieved in both the senior and veteran categories.
course_highlights: The Fjellhamar Relay has eight stages that give long-distance runners the opportunity to showcase their strength.
Bøler's runners achieved a time of 26:54 minutes, which resulted in 4th place in the senior men's category.
The relay is important for team selection for the Holmenkollen Relay and has resulted in several victories in the senior and veteran categories.

name: Baksjøløpet
description: The Baksjøløpet was first held in 1981 and is a traditional race that takes place every year in Åbogen in Eidskog. The main course is 11 km, which partly runs on gravel and asphalt roads, while participants who walk without timing can choose an alternative route of 6 km. The event mobilizes about 100 volunteers and attracts over 700 participants, creating a special atmosphere characterized by community spirit and togetherness. Showers and changing rooms are available, and the race is known for its friendly atmosphere and good organization.
course_highlights: The Baksjø race has a main route of 11 km, and participants can choose an alternative route of 6 km.
The event mobilizes more volunteers than there are people living in the village, which contributes to a unique and pleasant atmosphere.
The race costs only 150 kroner, making it accessible to many, and various prizes are awarded each year.

name: Oppdalskarusellen 1. løp
description: The Oppdal Carousel 1st race takes place on May 4, 2025, with the race starting at 2:00 PM. The registration deadline for the entire carousel is May 2, 2025, and more information, including registration, can be found on the carousel's own page. In 2020, Bjarte Bjertnæs won the race with a time of 10:15, and Maja Hval-Thomsen won the women's category with a time of 12:22.
course_highlights: Congratulations to the winners Mads Berge (10:05) and Helle Kristensen (12:33) in the 2025 edition of the race!
The Oppdal Carousel features several races throughout the year, with various distances and routes.
The race is part of a larger series that includes several competitions, giving participants the opportunity to compete for the overall victory.

name: Halden Byløp
description: Halden City Run is suitable for all ages with officially measured courses for 5 km and 10 km through the city center. There are 400/800/1500 m courses at Halden Stadium for children and youth. The start and finish line is inside Halden Stadium, and the 5 km loop is run twice for those participating in the 10 km. The course is mostly flat, except for a small hill just before the finish, allowing for fast times.
course_highlights: Halden City Run includes distances of 1500m, 5 km, and 10 km.
The course is well marked with course marshals at every intersection, ensuring a safe and clear racing experience.
Halden Sports Club, which was founded in 1912, organizes several track meets and is also the organizer of the City Race and the Cannon Race.

name: Fløibanen Opp
description: Fløibanen Opp is a spectacular uphill race taking place on April 20, 2026, when the Fløibanen is halted to give you the chance to make your way up to Fløyen along the tracks. This grueling race has a distance of approximately 820 meters with a brutal ascent of 310 meters in elevation, without any variation or breaks. The race offers an intense challenge in the heart of Bergen, and with limited spots available, it is an exclusive opportunity for both experienced runners and beginners looking to test their limits.
course_highlights: On April 20, 2026, the Fløibanen will be stopped for the only time of the year so that YOU can make your way up to Fløyen, along the tracks!
With a distance of approximately 820 meters and an elevation gain of 310 meters, the race offers an intense challenge in the heart of the city.
The audience has access along the entire course, creating an energetic and supportive atmosphere for the participants.

name: Stomperudkarusellen - løp
description: The Stomperud Carousel is a running series featuring 4 races that include various distances and laps, including the Bingen Loop at 5 km and the Aasgaard Loop. Shorter races are also organized, such as the 800 m on the track. This provides participants with the opportunity to choose a distance that suits their skill level.
course_highlights: The Stomperud Carousel includes several distances and laps, including the Light Trail, Aasgaard Loop, and Bingen Loop.
Shorter races are also organized, such as the 800 m on the track.

name: Terrengløpskarusell 1
description: The Athletics Group in Oppegård IL is also organizing a cross-country running series this year. The races are open to everyone, regardless of age and ambitions, and will take place on May 6, May 20, June 3, August 26, and September 9 at the Clubhouse, Østre Greverud. Participants can register for 200 NOK for all the races or 80 NOK per individual race. The cross-country races will take place during the training sessions for the athletics group's athletes, and there will be no regular training at Sofiemyr Stadium on the relevant days.
course_highlights: Before the 1st heat begins, there will be group warm-up sessions, where participants will run through the course, ensuring that everyone who is going to race becomes familiar with the layout of the course.

Distribution of race numbers will take place from the stage inside Haraldsvang starting at 5:00 PM, and we ask that the coaches for the groups take responsibility for distributing to their group to avoid congestion.
Oppegård IL Athletics encourages all children, young people, and adults of all ages to join this year's running carousel!

name: Ålgårdstafetten
description: Gjesdal IL invites you to the Ålgård Relay 2025 on Thursday, April 24. Registration must be completed by April 21, and the entry fee is 200 NOK per team with 4 legs and 300 NOK per team with 6 legs. For participants aged 13 and older, a yearly license or a one-time license purchase is required. The relay has categories for both children and adults, with legs of 1000, 1800, 470, 1400, 470, and 400 meters, and all exchanges take place at the athletics stadium or in the surrounding area.
course_highlights: The Ålgård Relay is a relay race where several people get their very first experience of running a leg at an adult age.
The relay's legs are adapted for both women and men, and the course consists of segments of 1000, 1800, 470, 1400, 470, and 400 meters.
In 2019, over a hundred teams participated, with Sandnes IL fielding 21 teams, and prizes were awarded to all participants up to 10 years old.

name: ASICS Sentrumsløpet
description: ASICS Sentrumsløpet is an annual race in Oslo with distances of 10 km, 5 km, and a children's race. The 10 km race is open to everyone who turns 12 in 2025 and older, while the 5 km race is for those who turn 10 in 2025 and older. The children's race is available for kids who turn 3-11 in 2025. The course for the 10 km starts on Karl Johans gate and includes hilly sections around Frognerparken, as well as an exciting route down towards Oslo City Hall.
course_highlights: The Sentrumsløpet traditionally starts on Karl Johans gate, with a tough uphill stretch towards the Palace.
The course runs in a loop around Frogner Park, where it is gently undulating with opportunities to make up time heading down towards Bygdøy Allé.
Along the way, there are several water stations, as well as lively streets that provide extra motivation for the final kilometers.

name: Røyse Ultra
description: Røyse Ultra is an annual ultramarathon held in Røyse, in the Hole municipality. The race was first organized in 2015, and it takes place in April. Participants run the Hytteplanmila eight times over the course of a day, totaling 80 km. The race consists of 10 kilometers every three hours, making it an ultra interval race.
course_highlights: The race was first held in 2015 and takes place in April.
The race is 8 x 10 km, as they run the Hytteplanmila eight times over the course of a day.
The race consists of running 10 kilometers every three hours, making it an ultra interval race.

name: Fjordkraft Bergen City Marathon
description: Welcome to the Fjordkraft Bergen City Marathon (FBCM) on Saturday, April 25, 2026. This will be the 15th edition of the race, and we look forward to another day filled with the joy of running, community, and urban life at its best. The start and finish line, as usual, will be at Bryggen, where the atmosphere sets the tone for a memorable experience. The course will take you through some of Bergen's most characteristic areas – from Old Bergen and the views along Fjellveien to the new walkway around Store Lungegårdsvann. The Bergen City Marathon 2026 offers a course filled with life, views, and the city's unique atmosphere.
course_highlights: On April 26, 19,000 running enthusiasts gathered to participate in the Fjordkraft Bergen City Marathon.
We are proud to be the main sponsor of a race that focuses on camaraderie, achievement, and inclusion.
The race provides support for a special cause through the event, with support for Downs Syndrome Westland in 2025.

name: Fevik Halvmaraton & 5km
description: We at IL Express hope you will come to Fevik Stadium on Saturday, April 27, as we are organizing the half marathon for the 19th time and the Fevik 5 km for the third time! We can offer a certified, fast, and easy-to-run course in a pleasant environment, making it suitable for both experienced runners looking to set a personal best and for first-timers in the half marathon. This is a race for everyone – it doesn't matter how long you expect to take – you are just as welcome regardless!
course_highlights: The half marathon route starts at Fevik Stadium and then continues via Strandsvingen, Moy Moner, Vik, Bringsværd, and further along the old railway line almost to Opplandsvegen.
The 5 km route starts at Fevik stadium at the same time as the half marathon and runs the same way towards Grimstad, before turning at Strand hotel.
The children's race starts at 12:40, and the kids will run one lap on the stadium. Everyone gets a medal.

description: The Siddisløpet is organized by the Sports Club Skjalg. Get ready for our spring running festival in Stavanger on April 26th! The Siddisløpet takes place around Store Stokkavannet, is 8.1 km long, and is suitable for those who have run a lot, run a little - or those in between! Sign up now!
course_highlights: The Siddisløpet is run around Store Stokkavannet.
The race is 8.1 km long.
Suitable for you who have run a lot, run a little - or you in between!

name: Monolittløpet
description: Welcome spring with a traditional trail run in spectacular surroundings along Iddefjorden in Halden. The Monolith Run is scheduled for April 25, 2026, and has become a tradition for many since the first race was held in 2013. Participants will experience 9 km of challenging yet scenic terrain, starting at the velodrome in Ystehede and finishing at the square in Halden city center. The course features significant elevation and some steep sections, but offers a fantastic nature experience. The race passes through areas where the raw stone for the Vigeland sculpture Monolith was quarried, reminding us of the important stone industry that provided livelihoods for many in the early 20th century.
course_highlights: The Monolith Race has already become a tradition for many, and there is good reason for that.
You can choose whether you want to run, jog, or walk the Monolith Race.
The route of the Monolith Run goes through the areas where the raw stone for the Vigeland sculpture, the Monolith, was quarried.

name: Backyard Ultra
description: Backyard Ultra is a form of ultramarathon where participants complete one lap (typically 4.167 km) every hour for as long as they can. There is no set distance for the race; it continues until only one participant remains. This format creates a unique challenge where both physical endurance and mental strength are crucial.
course_highlights: Participants complete one lap every hour, as long as they can.
There is no set distance for the race; it continues until there is only one participant left.
The format demands both physical endurance and mental strength.

name: Viggaløpet
description: The Viggaløpet is a recreational race between Brandbu and Gran, and has been organized since 1991. The race has its start and finish area in Gran and Brandbu every other year, and is a collaboration between Gran IL, Brandbu IF, Gran Shopping Center, and Brandbu Shopping Center. The Viggaløpet marks its 30th year, and although the traditional race was canceled, participants are encouraged to continue running.
course_highlights: The Vigga Race has been organized since 1991.
The race has its start and finish area in Gran and Brandbu every other year.
The Viggaløpet is a collaboration between Gran IL, Brandbu IF, Gran Shopping Center, and Brandbu Shopping Center.

name: Monolittstafetten
description: The Monolith Relay kicks off on April 25, 2026, and you can easily participate in both the Monolith Race and a relay leg on the same day! Bring your friends, gather your colleagues, or form a team with strangers – the most important thing is to have fun! Starting and finishing at the square in Halden, the 10 legs run along the fjord and around Hovsfjellet in beautiful nature. Each leg has varying lengths, elevation, and difficulty levels, making the race accessible to everyone.
course_highlights: The Monolith Relay is suitable for everyone, regardless of fitness level.
There are 10 stages that take place in beautiful surroundings along the fjord and around Hovsfjellet.
Buses are provided to transport participants back to the square after the exchange along the course.

name: Tveide Espe Rundt
description: Birkenes is the village where everything is supposed to be long and tough. A weekly meeting point is the race Espe Rundt, which is organized every Thursday during the summer months and also serves as a hiking trail for the rest of the week. Ivar Skåre is personally responsible for Espe Rundt, and the start line is at his garage door in Birkeland. This year, 104 participants took part in the run around the lake.
course_highlights: Espe Rundt is held every Thursday during the summer season.
The race also serves as a trail route on all the other days of the week.
104 participants have run around the lake this year.

name: Dogrun - Frognerparken
description: VOM DOGRUN is a pleasant activity for everyone who wants to be active together with their dog. Participants can choose to participate with or without timing, and the event is a social activity for the whole family. The start and finish are at the (old) Dog Meadow in Frogner Park, where participants can choose between two classes: Dogrun, which is a 7 km race with timing (two laps), and Dogwalk, which is a 3.5 km walk without timing.
course_highlights: The Vom Dogrun is a social activity for the whole family, for those who wish to walk, jog, or run with their dog.
The start and finish are at (old) Hundesletta in Frogner Park.
Classes: Dogrun: 7 km race with timing (two laps), Dogwalk: 3.5 km walk without timing.

name: Aron Opp
description: We are excited to present the fall's most intense challenge - Aron Opp! This is a hill climb race organized by Bedriftsidretten Buskerud and Vestfold in collaboration with Skimore Drammen and Arontunet Lodge. The start takes place at the bottom of the ski slope and follows the road in a loop up to the top, where the finish line is at the lift house. The course is approximately 1.7 km, where the fastest runners take about 10 minutes, and it takes 30-45 minutes at a brisk walk. New this year is the relay, which will be conducted in stages with a total of 5 legs of 350 meters each.
course_highlights: The course follows the gravel road in a loop along the ski slope from the bottom to the top.
The fastest runners complete the race in about 10 minutes, while it takes 30-45 minutes to walk up.
The relay consists of 5 legs, each measuring 350 meters.

name: Begbyløpet
description:
On Sunday, April 26, 2026, at 12:00 PM, a 10 km race will start in hilly terrain on gravel and asphalt in beautiful surroundings in Begby, Fredrikstad. Timing will be provided by EQ timing.

At 11:00 AM, a 1 km race for children up to 12 years old will begin (this race is free).
additional: There is a mass start for women and men, meeting at the Begby clubhouse.
course_highlights: 10 km for the biggest and 1 km for the smallest.
Save the date and stay tuned for information about registration.
Release an exciting race course.

name: Jæren Sparebank Sentrumsløp
description: On Tuesday, April 29, Gjesdal IL invites you to the brand new Jæren Sparebank City Run in Ålgård center. Participants can choose between two distances: 700 meters and 5 kilometers, with the 5 km run taking place on a 1.25 km loop that is repeated four times. The start and finish are on Torgveien, and the course goes over the completely new Liv Godin bridge. The course is flat and nice, with large sections on gravel.
course_highlights: Participants can choose between two distances: 700 meters and 5 kilometers.
The course is 1.25 km long and is run 4 times.
There is a special offer at Norwegian Outlet Stavanger for participants who show their race number after the event.

name: Terrengløpskarusellen løp
description: The Cross-Country Running Carousel Race 1 is part of a series of three races organized by Haugesund Idrettslag. The courses mostly run on gravel paths, but there is some terrain with forest cover (approximately 200m per lap on the 620m courses). The start and finish for all courses are at the stage/pavilion inside Haraldsvang, and there will be an awards ceremony after the final race from the stage in Haraldsvang.
course_highlights: Race numbers are distributed by class on stage inside Haraldsvang by the coaches.
It is important that the participants take care of their race number throughout all three races.
The cross-country running series has been a tradition since 1972 and has seen a growing interest over the years.

name: Sørdalskarusellen Kringsjåløpet
description: The Kringsjåløpet is 2.71 km long and starts and finishes at Nordre Ål school. The start is on Gamle Kringsjåvei on the bridge over Skurva right by Nordre Ål school, and the route follows Kringsjåveien northward, takes the footpath down to Ekromskogen, goes through the upper section southward, and follows Teigveien back to Nordre Ål school. The race is being organized for the 43rd time in 2024, featuring both a mass start and a virtual race. The results will be sent to Kondis.no for statistical recording.
course_highlights: There will be a virtual race from Saturday to Tuesday and a mass start on Wednesday, April 24th at 7:00 PM.
Hoka will have a booth in the start area with great offers, and Sport 1 is sponsoring sports drinks for all participants at the finish line.
The course is officially measured at 3 km, but this year it is 70 meters shorter than last year.

name: Søndagsløpet Sarpsborg
description: The Sunday Run is a popular race that takes place in Kalnesskogen in the municipality of Sarpsborg, and was started in 2014. The race is held every Sunday from April to mid-October, featuring three courses of varying lengths: the yellow at 7.05 km, the green at 8.87 km, and the red at 10.2 km. The courses vary in difficulty, with the red course having steep climbs, especially between 5 and 6 km. The Sunday Run is free to participate in and is suitable for all levels, from recreational runners to elite athletes.
course_highlights: The race has three different courses: yellow, green, and red, each offering unique challenges for various levels of runners.
Participants can expect well-organized conditions, with opportunities to set personal records and compete against others.
The Sunday race is free to participate in and has been a part of the running community in Sarpsborg for many years.

name: Grue Halvmaraton
description: Grue Half Marathon is a race that takes place in Grue, Norway, on May 1, 2024. Participants have a maximum time of 2:30 hours, and the race accounts for train crossings. There will be 6 aid stations evenly distributed along the course, with energy drinks and water available. The course has pace setters for different finishing times, and all participants will receive a medal.
course_highlights: The race includes both men's and women's classes for the half marathon as well as 10 kilometers.
Participants can expect a challenging and scenic course.
There are 6 aid stations evenly distributed along the course.

name: mailøpet
description: We welcome you to the mail race on May 11 and the junior festival on May 12, where both races start at 8:00 AM. The 58th mail race had great running weather and good conditions for both runners and spectators, with a total of 141 participants, including 38 in junior, senior, and veteran classes. The men's winner was Vetle Uhre Hammersvik from Førde with a time of 9:55, while the women's winner was Eli Karin Sjåstad Åsebø from Volda with a time of 14:08.
course_highlights: It was the young man Vetle Uhre Hammersvik from Førde, but with close roots from Selje, who decided the 1st mail race of 2016 in a fierce duel against last year's champion Eirik Voksøy Bringvor from Sandsøy, winning by just one second.
We welcome you to the mail race on May 11 and the junior festival on May 12. Entrance is 150,- per day or 200,- for the whole weekend. Children under 12 get in for free.
The men's winner this year, as last year, was Vetle Uhre Hammersvik from Førde with a strong time of 9:55. The women's winner was Eli Karin Sjåstad Åsebø from Volda with 14:08.

name: Strandamilå
description: Strandamilå 2023 was held for the 43rd time and was finally back as a family race! Despite less than favorable weather conditions, there was an impressive turnout with over 550 participants across all distances, and the registration nearly matched the best numbers of the last 15 years with 125 sign-ups. We are very pleased with the event and look forward to new heights next year! Stay tuned on social media for photos from the race when they are ready.
course_highlights: Strandamilå has proud traditions dating back to 1980 and is always held on May 1st.
Over 550 participants in all our distances is very good, and the Strandamilå itself matched the best registration in the last 15 years with 125 sign-ups.

This day is filled with laughter, crazy experiences, and positivity, and we leave all our everyday tasks at home. The Girls' Run is a low-threshold race that promises an unforgettable running celebration for women, having gathered up to 12,000 participants, which creates a festive atmosphere and engagement in the local community.
course_highlights: The Girls' Run is a hugely popular event that has gathered up to 12,000 participants.
The event creates a festive atmosphere and engagement in the local community.
The surface for running is primarily gravel, with some asphalt, set in scenic surroundings.

name: Skogvokteren Ultra
description: Welcome to the fourth edition of the Skogvokteren Ultra! This is a low-threshold, unmarked race with 100% trail magic, where we gather in the forests of Grenland to celebrate spring and compete for honor and glory. Skogvokting is about appreciating the local environment, community, and celebrating the ability to move efficiently through the terrain. We hope to see you sharp and ready at five o'clock on Saturday, May 4, 2024, when the race kicks off in Porsgrunn.
course_highlights: The Skogvokteren Ultra is Grenland's annual ultra celebration with a low-threshold and authentic profile on spring trails during the transition from April to May.
The race is a UTMB Index event at 100K with a distance of 88.00 km and an elevation gain of 3700 meters.
We focus on mastery and progression, but we also facilitate performance.

description: On Tuesday, the famous beach race took place in Etape Bornholm, which is quite unique in its kind. It is the shortest of the stage races, only 5.8 kilometers long, but also the most difficult and challenging for many. 4 of the kilometers are on sandy beach along the water's edge or in loose sand dunes, much like in a desert. Either you really like this very special race, or you hate it.
course_highlights: Norwegian Vikings, however, mastered the unusual terrain very well.
The course turns inward and through the large sand dunes, up and down in the loose sand, until some steep inclines must be tackled.

description: Askøy lengthwise is a long trail with very varied terrain, where our volunteer team continually improves the path. There are still wet and muddy sections along the way, but large parts of the trail run on nice paths and hiking trails. In the northern part of the island, some smaller sections of the distance are on asphalt, such as at Skråmestø and from the water tower at Merkesvik to Herdlabroen. All participants take part at their own risk and should make a conscious decision in advance about whether they are fit enough to walk or run such a long distance. The route will be marked from start to finish with red pictograms and ribbons.

description: Wings for Life World Run is a unique race where participants run to support research on spinal cord injuries. The race does not have a fixed distance; instead, participants run as far as they can before being caught by a "Catcher Car." This creates an exciting and dynamic experience, as all participants start at the same time, but the goal is to run as far as possible before the car catches up with them. 100% of the entry fee goes directly to the Wings for Life Foundation to fund research.

description: Eikenosa Opp is a mountain race in Ålesund organized by Emblem IL. The race was first held in 2004 and starts at about 2 meters above sea level at the bottom of Eikenosvågen, 18 km east of Ålesund city center. The course is 4.5 km long and runs on asphalt and gravel roads, finishing at the west end of the dam at Røssevollsvatnet at 295 meters. The men's course record is 17 minutes and 55 seconds, set by Johan Bugge in 2019, while the women's record is 22 minutes and 3 seconds by Ingrid Festøs from 2017.

name: 4625 Løpet
description: The 4625 race is a new event being held for the first time in 2024. We want to invite YOU to help create a running celebration on the island! 4625 is the postal code for Flekkerøya, the gem located at the edge of the sea on the way to Denmark from Kristiansand. The island is a popular spot for running, with varied terrain and countless picture-perfect viewpoints, providing a perfect foundation for a fun and memorable course, whether you're running for the first time or competing at the front of the elite class.
course_highlights: The race features a slightly hilly course on Flekkerøy, which is known for its beautiful scenery.
It became a grand community celebration with 165 children and 180 adults participating in the very first edition of the race.
Benjamin Andersen, leader of the Flekkerøy Running Club, expressed his happiness over the successful execution of the race.

images.alt_text: Runner on a trail course. Beautiful nature. 4625 race.

name: Prestfoss Stafetten
description: Welcome to the traditional PRESTFOSS RELAY, which takes place on May 17th at 18:25! The relay has a history that dates back to 1929, and this year we celebrate 90 years since the first event. Modum FIK participated with 4 teams, with the girls taking home the trophy for the second year in a row, while the boys were defeated by Sigdal 1 and 2. It was an exciting finish that the audience greatly appreciated, with enthusiastic cheers.
course_highlights: The women's team from Eggedal ran fast and was a great source of entertainment as they topped the show class in the Prestfoss relay.
The weather is forecasted to be glorious on May 17th this year, so there's nothing to do but look forward to it!
The success with classes in business and show will be repeated this year as well.

images.alt_text: Runners in the Prestfoss relay. Great atmosphere and beautiful weather.

Prestfoss Relay 2024 results. 22 teams participated.

name: Grefsenkollen Opp
description: Nydalens Skiklub is pleased to invite you once again to the OBOS Grefsenkollen Uphill on May 25th! This uphill race in Oslo is filled with running enthusiasts, fast legs, and great energy. The course starts at Muselunden by Sinsenkrysset at an elevation of 110 meters and ascends to the top of Grefsenkollen at 380 meters above sea level, with a total distance of 4.5 km. Parking is limited, so we recommend using public transport.
course_highlights: Grefsenkollen Uphill has the full distance start at 09:40 and the children's race starts at 10:25.
The route goes through the city streets of Grefsen before it turns up the steep Grefsenkollveien, and features asphalt as the surface all the way.
All results will be available LIVE at Racedays, which also handles timing and registration.

name: Endless Shore Ultra
description: Welcome to the ultimate coastal trail from Jeløy in Østfold to Nesodden in Akershus! This race offers an unforgettable journey through some of the most scenic landscapes on this side of Eastern Norway, featuring a mix of runnable coastal trails, rocky beaches, winding roots, beautiful pine forests, charming towns, dense woods, and stunning views. Endless Shore Ultra offers distances of 50 and 100 miles and is open for registration for both novice and experienced runners.
course_highlights: This race offers an unforgettable journey through some of the most scenic landscapes on this side of Eastern Norway.
It is a mix of easily runnable coastal paths, rocky beaches, winding roots, beautiful pine forests, charming villages, dense woods, and fantastic views.
Endless Shore Ultra is open for registration for both novice and seasoned runners.

images.alt_text: Beautiful coastal village, suitable for the Endless Shore Ultra course.

name: Hamarløpet
description: Hamarløpet is a 10-kilometer street race through the beautiful surroundings of the inland town of Hamar. The purpose of Hamarløpet is to contribute to public health by motivating both young and old to lead active lives. The race aims to be an arena for both the fastest runners and those who typically do not participate in other racing events, encouraging a joy of activity without prestige. Organized by the Hamarløpet Association, this is an ideal initiative where any profits go to charitable causes.
course_highlights: The course for the Hamarløpet is a flat and officially measured 10-kilometer route that runs along beautiful paths by Lake Mjøsa, starting from Hamar city center.
The start and finish line are at Skibladnerbrygga, and the race goes through Koigen, Domkirkeodden, Strandveien, and the two railway underpasses.
There will be a water station and split time at 5 km, and the race will take place on Saturday, May 23 at 1:00 PM.

name: Sandefjordsløpet
description: Welcome to the Sandefjord Race on Saturday, May 23, 2026. The race is organized by STIF for the 47th time in 2026, featuring a course that is 5 km long, with the start and finish in Badeparken. For the 10 km distance, two laps will be run, and the course is officially measured with a course certificate from DNM/NFIF. There will be a water station in Badeparken, at the finish line for the 5 km and halfway through the race for the 10 km, and each kilometer is marked with a green circle.
course_highlights: The course is 5 km long, with the start and finish in Badeparken.
In the 10 km distance, two laps are run.
The course has been officially measured and has a course certificate from DNM/NFIF.

name: Vassøy Backyard Ultra
description: Vassøy Backyard Ultra is a unique ultramarathon that takes place on the beautiful island of Vassøy. Runners must complete a lap of 6.7 kilometers each hour, and there is no set distance – runners continue to run as long as they can. This race combines both physical and mental endurance, and it is a fantastic experience for both participants and spectators.
course_highlights: The runners must complete a lap of 6.7 kilometers every hour.
There is no set distance – the runners keep running as long as they can.
The race combines both physical and mental endurance.

name: Saudafjellet Marathon
description: Welcome to a truly unique half marathon and marathon over Saudafjellet – one of Norway's most spectacular mountain crossings! The race starts in Røldal and ascends the mountain between high snowbanks and rugged mountain scenery, finishing at the town square in the heart of Sauda. Along the route, you can expect world-class architecture and an unparalleled nature experience, as the path winds through magnificent mountain landscapes, deep valleys, and roaring waterfalls.
course_highlights: Start in Røldal and up the mountain between high snowbanks and rugged mountain scenery.
Finish line at the town square in the middle of Sauda center.
A unique nature experience, with a road winding through magnificent mountain landscapes, deep valleys, and roaring waterfalls.

images.alt_text: Runner in the terrain during the Saudafjellet Marathon, showcasing the course's mountainous landscape.
Beautiful landscape in Norway with mountains, lakes, and green meadows. Perfect for trail running.
