description: Haglebu Backyard Ultra is an ultramarathon event taking place on August 23, 2025, with the start and finish at Haglebu Feriesenter. Participants must complete as many laps as possible of 6706 meters each hour, with a new lap starting every 60 minutes. There is a maximum of 12 laps, and the first man and woman to finish the last lap win the race. Everyone who completes at least one lap will receive a medal, and there will also be raffle prizes.

name: Drøbakløpet
description: The Drøbak Race replaces the traditional Blomstermila and has changed both the course layout and the start/finish location to Drøbak Torg. The race takes place in August, after the school year begins, to avoid competition with the end of school and vacation plans. The course runs from Drøbak Torg, through Kirkegata and Badeparken, past Drøbak Church, and ends up in Storgata. Parts of the course will be closed off to ensure traffic safety, but arrangements will be made for the town center to remain lively that afternoon.

The course follows the coastal path along the water, with a turnaround at the kiosk on Steinbrygga, before taking you out of the woods by the treatment plant and back to Horten via the coastal path. This race offers you the chance to experience stunning natural scenery while challenging yourself in a half marathon.

description: Vikerfjell Challenge is an exciting running experience with fantastic nature encounters and challenging courses. Participants can choose between three distances: 21 km, 11 km, and a 2.5 km children's race. The courses run on gravel roads, trails, and in terrain, so be prepared to get your feet wet. The longest distance starts from Ringerudsetra and ends at Skarrudsetra, while the 11 km course starts from Tossviksetra.

The course runs on gravel roads, trails, and in terrain, so be prepared to get your feet wet.

name: Nipkollen Challenge
description: The Nipkollen Challenge is not just any race – it’s a raw experience through Nannestad's most beautiful and challenging terrain. This is not about fast asphalt kilometers, but about mastering technical trails, steep ascents, and undulating stretches that truly test you. Three distances – one common challenge: 14 km for all ages, 25 km for the tough, and 50 km for the truly dedicated, which is one of Norway's toughest ultramarathons. The race offers participants the chance to test their skills in a spectacular setting, with views that reward the effort.

The course follows a route that was used during World War II to help people escape the country, and runs between Enebakk/Øyeren and Skullerud in Oslo. This race is incredibly fun and challenging, providing participants with a unique experience in scenic surroundings.

From about 35 km, participants follow the marathon course all the way to the finish, with a tough ending up the notorious Kamfossbakken, which has an average incline of 10% over 3 km. This race takes place in the foothills of Jotunheimen and includes an incorporated uphill race.

name: Mud Monkey 2025
description:
MUDMONKEY 2025

Welcome to the Jungle. Play Dirty. Laugh Louder.

Mud. Obstacles. Screams and laughter. This is not a race – this is the jungle's playground for adults (and teenagers who aren't afraid to slip in style).

MudMonkey 2025 invites you to a day of total bananas in nature: climbing, crawling, water, fire, and a bunch of race-crazy Monkeys who live to challenge you through the course. Forget asphalt and fences – here you face the jungle's resistance with a grin.

MUDMONKEY 5K – “Monkey Business in Battle Mode”

5 kilometers with 25 technical and natural obstacles. 
You climb, tumble, crawl, and laugh your way through the mud while unruly MudMonkeys try to block you – physically. 
Go solo or as a tribe – but one thing is for sure: You will emerge covered in mud and full of adrenaline.

Age limit: 13+

A parental declaration must be signed before the start (sent via email the week before the race).

MUDMONKEY 8K – “Mud Mayhem and Jungle Fury”

8 kilometers. 40+ obstacles.

When you think it can't get wilder, you arrive here. 
This is the highlight of the obstacle race: mud pits, zip lines, icy water, flames, slippery stones – and of course, crazy MudMonkeys trying to topple you with laughter and resistance.

Age limit: 16+

A declaration must be signed before the start (sent via email the week before the race).

____________________________________________________________________________________

COMING 2026 – MUDMONKEY EXTREME 21K

“For those who have never been dirty enough”

21 km. 70+ obstacles. Here you will meet your limits – and have them shattered.

Spectator-friendly, but participant-hostile course full of fire, ice, mud, and monkey madness.

Only for the most bananas among us.

Age limit: 18+
A declaration must be signed before the start (sent via email the week before the race).

EVERYONE GETS A MEDAL – NO ONE GOES HOME DRY OR CLEAN!!

Here, competition is held in individual classes and in tribes (teams). 
The fastest will be celebrated with honor and glory – but everyone who finishes gets a medal and the right to call themselves a true MudMonkey.
additional: Feel free to call us at 95961803 or send an email to hei@xchallenge.no.

name: Sognefjord Trail Run
description:
Join the Sognefjord Trail Run 2025! A spectacular trail race set in the majestic landscape of the Sognefjord - Norway's longest and deepest fjord.

Choose between 13, 23, or 43 km and experience technical trails, flowing paths, and stunning surroundings. The race is suitable for both experienced runners and beginners – big and small.

You will become part of an inclusive community, with social activities in the mountain sports village of Sogndal on both Friday and Saturday evenings.

Sign up now – and be part of an extraordinary racing experience! 🏃‍♀️⛰️🌟
course_highlights: The route passes Fanaråken, home to the highest cabin in Norway (2068 m a.s.l.).
On clear days, the summit of Galdhøpiggen offers a fantastic view of the western part of Jotunheimen.
Choose between distances of 13KM, 21KM, 42KM, or join the kids' race.

The starting point is at Falck Nutec in Gravdal, with the finish line at the top of Lyderhorn, 396 meters above sea level. The course is approximately 3.8 km, and all school students in the Laksevåg district are offered the opportunity to participate for free.

The race takes place on September 28th in Bygnes, Karmøy, and has a Norse mythology theme. There will be an adult race, a family race, and a children's race, and the event is designed to be accessible for everyone, from beginners to elite athletes. Corporate teams, sports clubs, and bachelor parties can also register.

This race is for everyone, and participants are divided into heats based on their expected finish times, providing a golden opportunity for fast times, whether you are chasing a personal record or the national championship requirement. With 25 flat laps without a single meter of elevation, the organizers promise a fantastic day dedicated to running and community, with a great atmosphere and festive surroundings.

On this day, you will use all your strength and experience a nature adventure you will not soon forget.

description: Kolbotnvannet Rundt features a course in scenic surroundings on terrain, gravel, and asphalt. You can participate with or without timing, with distances of 5 km and 10 km. The start is at Kolbotn Torg, and the route includes asphalt, forest trails, and gravel, with a finish line after 5 km. There is also a family event with a shorter loop of about 2 km, perfect for strollers.

name: Styrkeprøven Rett Vest
description: Styrkeprøven Rett Vest is an ultramarathon held in the mountains of Bergen on the last weekend of August. The course, which stretches approximately 45 km from Gullbotn to Kjøkkelvik, has a total elevation gain of over 3000 meters and includes several peaks such as Gullfjellstoppen and Ulriken. Since its inception in 1984, this event has become an annual tradition for many running enthusiasts, with course records of 4 hours and 40 minutes for men and 6 hours and 3 minutes for women. In 2023, Styrkeprøven Rett Vest celebrated its 35th anniversary.
course_highlights: The route starts at Gullbotn and ascends to the summit of Gullfjell, which is the highest point of the route at 987 meters.
The course has a total elevation gain of over 3000 meters, providing a challenging and scenic experience.
Styrkeprøven Rett Vest is composed of volunteer members focused on creating a healthy and motivating activity event.

Each race is announced on Friday at 12:00, and the course is open until Sunday at 11:00 the following weekend, with a mass start precisely at 11:00. The course is certified to be as close to 10 km as possible.

name: Flemstubben
description: The Flemstubben race is an annual road race held in Flemma, and this year it was conducted for the 44th time with 140 participants. The race has a distance of 10 kilometers, and Johan Bugge from Eidsvåg IL was the pre-race favorite, delivering a time of 30:52, just 6 seconds behind his own course record. Live Johannessen Solheimdal from Steinkjer FIK smashed her own record with an impressive time of 34:41, while Morten Eilifsen from Averøy Running Club achieved the second-best overall time with 34:35.

The courses mainly go on trails, featuring both uphill and downhill sections, and it's allowed to jump in the puddles! The races are free, and on-site registration is possible up to 15 minutes before the start. Everyone receives a bib number, and at the finish line, there will be juice and a medal waiting.

The races are free, and you can sign up by following the link below.

name: Knarvik Halvmaraton
description: Knarvik Half Marathon starts and finishes in the same place inside Knarvik Stadium. The course runs on roads in Knarvik and into the Brekkeløypa, where there is gravel, while the rest of the course is on asphalt. There are 8 aid stations along the route, and after crossing the finish line inside the stadium, water and bananas will be served. The course is well marked with approximately 20 course marshals present, and the Red Cross will also be on-site. The half marathon consists of 4 laps of the 5 km course, with an additional distance of 1097 meters onto the walkway towards Gjervik.
course_highlights: The course is car-free and offers participants beautiful scenery along the way.
There are 8 aid stations along the course, and after finishing, water and bananas will be served.
The age limit for participation is 15 years.

The rest of the course is on asphalt, with one water station along the way. The course is well marked, car-free, and the Red Cross will be present for safety. The date of the race is Saturday, September 6, starting at 1:30 PM.

name: Track & Glow 10k
description: Track & Glow 10k is organized at Gjesdal Sports Park, which is the second running track in Norway with Wavelight technology. Heat and wave setup will be announced soon, and lap counting will occur automatically in EQ-timing's system, which will display on the big screen how many laps you have completed. This race offers a unique opportunity to experience running with modern technology in a beautiful setting.
course_highlights: The second running track in Norway with Wavelight technology.
Lap counting will occur automatically in EQ-timing's system.
Heat and heat setup will be coming soon here.

name: Numedalsløpet
description: The Numedalsløpet was first held in 1936 and is thus one of the oldest sports events in Numedal. The race takes place on easy forest terrain from Høgheim in Lyngdal to Flesberg Community House and is approximately 13 km long. It is a race for both competitive runners and recreational joggers, organized in collaboration with Lyngdal and Svene Sports Clubs.
course_highlights: The race was first held in 1936 with 100 participants and has a long history.
The Numedalsløpet has a distance of approximately 13 km and takes place in easy forest terrain.
It is a race for both competitive runners and recreational participants, making it accessible for all levels.

name: Romsdalseggenløpet
description: The Romsdalseggen Race is a mountain run set in majestic surroundings, starting in Vengesdalen and finishing at the top of Nesaksla. During the journey across the mountain, you can expect both a thrilling sensation in your stomach and lactic acid in your legs, but above all, a fantastic experience with magnificent peaks like Vengetindene, Romsdalshorn, and Trolltindene surrounding you. The course is 8.6 km long, with 970 meters of positive elevation gain and 700 meters of negative elevation, and features exciting and challenging sections equipped with safety measures for secure passage.
course_highlights: The route offers a fantastic view with magnificent mountains such as Vengetindene, Romsdalshorn, and Trolltindene.
The course includes 4 different secured sections with chains to help participants navigate the challenging areas.
The exciting and challenging part begins when you reach the ridge, with 4.6 adrenaline-pumping kilometers remaining.

name: Furusjøen Rundt-løpet
description: The race starts at Rudland Fjellsenter and goes 500 meters on asphalted road towards Bjørgebu. Then the route follows Peer-Gynt Seterveg and turns towards Årvillingen, before it goes through easy, flat terrain along Årvillingen and further towards Hovde on gravel road to the first aid station. The route continues towards Fryosen and Frylisætra, and further to Luseby, Glitra, and Pungen, where the second aid station is located. After several gravel roads and scenic surroundings, the race concludes at Rudland Fjellsenter.
course_highlights: Trail running in enchanting surroundings, with a dedicated course for children and recreational runners.
Fun runs that can also be done as a march - for those who find it adventurous to be outdoors in beautiful nature alone or with friends, family, or colleagues.
The course follows a gravel road for about 3 km up towards Haugsetra, passing old mountain farm cabins, before descending again via Rustugusetra towards the finish.

description: The Elvelangsløpet 2023 takes place on Saturday, September 9, and invites you to an exciting race on the new hiking trail in Ål. The course is 4000 m long with small elevation changes, and there are separate courses for children and youth. The event includes distances of 400 meters for children, 1400 meters for youth, and 4000 meters for juniors, seniors, and veterans. The start and finish are at the new athletics track at Bråta, and participation is free with simple prizes.
course_highlights: Course record: Ladies 15:45 (Olivia Opheim) and Men 12:58 (Jonas Grøsland).
The event has a dedicated course for children and youth with distances of 0.4 km and 1.4 km.
The distribution of race numbers takes place right by the start at Bråta, with parking available.

The course for 2024 is just as tough and fun as always, with a length of approximately 6 km and over 40 challenging obstacles. It is designed so that everyone can finish and experience a sense of achievement, with the option of 5 burpees as an alternative if an obstacle is too difficult. You can participate individually or as a team, and choose your starting wave and time.

The course is designed so that everyone can finish and that everyone will definitely experience a sense of achievement.

name: Bodøryggen
description: On Saturday, October 1st, the Bodø Run Bodøryggen will take place, a majestic mountain race of approximately 21 kilometers from Skaug on the Nordsia of Bodø to Bestemorenga in the heart of Bodømarka. This mountain race features an elevation gain of 1000 meters, and the maximum number of participants is 200. The course is officially measured, and the steep ascent to Skaugtuva (626 m.a.s.l.) offers a fantastic view that can be enjoyed along the Bodøryggen.

name: Balestrand Opp og Rundt
description: Balestrand Up and Around 2025 is a timed competition that stretches over 9 km, starting and finishing at Kreklingen Stadium. The route goes from Kreklingen Stadium up to about 400 meters above sea level, where there is a relatively flat path to the day cabin "Balabu" and further to Fjærestadstølen. After that, the route descends on a developed path and forest road before returning to Kreklingen Stadium. Additionally, there is a non-timed fitness class of 6 km, where participants can choose their start time between 09:00 and 11:30 on Saturday, September 6th.

name: Finnskogløpet
description: The Finnskogløpet was held this year in collaboration between Lunderseter IL and Kongsvingerkarusellen. This was also the 7th race in this year's series, where the participants ran 9.3 km on the course, which was used for the first time during last year's Finnskogløp. The winner, Per Erik Monsrud from Austmarka, set a new record with a time of 33:59, while Christine Nybråten was once again the best among the women with a record time of 40:32. A total of 63 participants lined up at the start.
course_highlights: The winner of the Finnskogløpet was Per Erik Monsrud, who, with a time of 33:59, beat last year's record by almost three minutes.
Christine Nybråten has been the best woman in all the series races she has participated in this year, with a record time of 40.32.
The 12-year-old Eivind Duelien Vaaje finished with the fourth best time of all participants at 36.43, also breaking the old course record.

description: Trysilrypa is this year's women's weekend in Trysil, where thousands of women gather to enjoy the autumn-clad Trysil Mountain. Participants can choose between 6, 10, and 13 km, either as a race or a hiking march, with all routes taking place in beautiful high mountain terrain, starting and finishing at SkiStar Lodge in Fageråsen. This is Norway's largest mountain race and march for women, and the event is suitable for everyone, regardless of fitness level.

name: Nordmarkstravern
description: Nordmarkstravern is a genuine forest race in Nordmarka, held on the first Saturday in September. The race features a varied and scenic route, with several distances available for participants, including Heltravern at 30 km, Halvtravern at 15 km, Kvarttraverner at 7 km, and Trillerner at 6 km. The race starts at Stryken and goes through Nordmarka, finishing at Kringsjå, with transport to the start arranged by buses from Sognsvann.
course_highlights: Nordmarkstravern was founded in 1972, and in 2022 the race was held for the 50th time.
Heltraverner 30 km runs on trails and gravel roads from Stryken to Kringsjå by Sognsvann, a classic journey through some of Nordmarka's most beautiful areas.
The Quarter Trotter 7 km is intended for the youngest participants, preferably accompanied by a mother or father, and features a course that includes 2.5 km on trails.

name: Blodslitet
description: Blodslitet is an orienteering race, long-distance, ultra-long-distance, organized every year by Fredrikstad Ski Club. This race is the oldest local race still held in Ålesund and takes place early in the fall, usually in September. In 2025, the race will take place on Wednesday, September 10 at 6:00 PM, starting at the top of Fagerlia with a total length of 6.71 km. The course includes tough uphill sections but becomes easier towards the end, and trophies are awarded to the best female and male runners.
course_highlights: The race has a long history dating back to the early 1980s, with the first event in Blodslitet in 1982.
The course record for men is 23:07, set by Lars Roger Lundanes in 1985, while the women's record is 24:35 by Live Johannessen Solheimdal (2023).
Around 2000 participants from all over Scandinavia take part, and Blodslitet has established a strong reputation as a top-quality event.

The course offers varied terrain and fantastic nature, making it a unique experience for both experienced runners and beginners. The Sumarkarusellen Holavatnet Rundt was first held in 1983 and is now in its 41st season, with about 130 participants showing up every Wednesday to exercise on the scenic route.
course_highlights: The route goes around Holavatnet on asphalt and gravel paths, and it's easy to take a stroller along the loop.
The race features varied terrain, providing a unique experience for both experienced runners and beginners.

name: Espe Rundt Finale
description: Espe Rundt is a 7 km fitness run held weekly from Easter to the moose hunt, starting from Nordåsveien 43 in Birkeland. The race is unique as the presumed weakest participant can break the finish line first in the final, which takes place on September 22. The course, which is 7050 m long, is challenging and includes varied terrain such as asphalt, gravel roads, forest paths, marshes, hills, and rocky sections. The organizer has conducted the race over 650 times since its inception in 1989.
course_highlights: Anyone who has completed 3 timed races in the year can participate in the final.
The course is considered very challenging and includes all types of terrain.
Everyone has an equal chance of winning, as the one who runs the latest starts first in the final.

course_highlights: Fast and flat course, designed for records. AIMS-certified course.
Results available immediately after finishing.
The race takes place on a scenic route that allows participants to enjoy the surroundings while they compete.

name: Lina Roindt
description: Lina Roindt is a road race that takes place on September 18, starting and finishing at Torshall in Bolme, Rindal. The competitive runners completed a lap of 10.8 km around Rindal center, while recreational participants could choose between two options: one lap around Rinnvollen (3 km) and one around the center via Sunnabrua (6.7 km). This year, a total of 295 people participated, making it the largest starting field since 1993. Lina Roindt is known as the big family day, with high participation and an efficient recreational committee.
course_highlights: Great participation in the Lina Roindt, with 238 in the fun run category without timing and 25 in the competitive categories, totaling 263 participants.
42 of the participants lined up in the starting field that raced for time, the largest starting field since 1993.
There was excitement about whether Strindheim runner Ebrahim Abdulaziz could break the nearly 30-year-old course record set by Dag Øxnvad.

name: Frogn på langs
description: Frogn Longways 2025 takes place on Sunday, September 14, and is a cultural hiking march and trail run for the whole family. The route goes through varying forest and cultural landscapes via historical sites in Frogn, providing a great opportunity to get to know the municipality. Drinks will be served at five checkpoints, but it is recommended to bring your own drinks and packed lunch for those who wish to complete the entire route. Participants can choose to start from Ramme or Follo Museum, and the trail run starts at 10:00 AM with distances of 10 or 28 km.
course_highlights: The route goes through varying forest and cultural landscapes via historical sites in Frogn, and is a great opportunity to get to know our beautiful municipality.
Drinks will be served at the five refreshment stations, but we still recommend that you, as a walker, bring your own drinks and packed lunch.
Frogn along the way is a massive public health initiative, and the organizers have put in a lot of effort to ensure that participants can enjoy top-notch trails.

name: Moovløpet
description: Welcome to the Moov Race on September 15th in Drammen! This is a low-threshold race with a flat and nice course profile, starting and finishing at the Ypsilon Bridge. The children's race starts at 10:00 AM, and all participants receive a medal. The mass start for the 5 km and 10 km races is at 11:00 AM. The entry fee is 250 NOK for non-members, while Moov members participate for free.
course_highlights: Children's race with a medal for all participants at 10:00.
Mass start for 5 km and 10 km at 11:00.
Low-threshold running with a great atmosphere.

name: Dokkarunden
description: The Dokkarunden is an exciting race that takes participants through beautiful and varied landscapes. The course is 10 km long and is perfect for both beginners and experienced runners. Participants will have the opportunity to experience nature up close, with several highlights along the route, including spectacular views and challenging terrain. The race takes place on Sunday, September 15, 2024, at 1:00 PM from Dokka Stadium.
course_highlights: The course is 10 km long and is perfect for both beginners and experienced runners.
Participants will have the opportunity to experience nature up close.
There are several highlights along the route, including spectacular views and challenging terrain.

name: Seterløpet
description: Seterløpet, Norway's oldest race, is organized from Solumsmoen in Sigdal to Vestre Spone Sports Ground. The race, which is 18.5 km long, has a mass start for competitive runners at 11:00 AM, while recreational runners can start from 9:00 AM. There is organized transportation from Vestre Spone Sports Ground at around 9:30 AM, and registration takes place at the start. This race is a collaboration between Nedre Sigdal Sports Club and Vestre Spone IF.
course_highlights: The Seterløpet was first held in 1936 and is thus Norway's oldest race.
The race has a mass start for the competitive class at 11:00 AM, while recreational runners can start from 9:00 AM.
There is organized transportation from Vestre Spone sports field to the starting location.

name: Dalajoggen Høst
description: Dalajoggen Autumn takes place on May 16, where you can walk, jog, or cycle around Sagslotten and participate in a draw for great prizes. The start is at 6:00 PM from the Youth House, and the course consists of one or two laps of 5 and 10 km. If you wish to run for time, you can register via the link: https://live.eqtiming.com/72350#dashboard. For only NOK 200, you can also sign up for all our races, and it's free for children under 16 years old.

The course consists of one or two laps of 5 and 10 km.

Around 60 active runners of all ages participated in the race at Stavsjø, some in the 10-kilometer and others in the 5-kilometer. Cecilie Kvehaugen Hansen was among the participants, and she expressed joy that there are competitions for everyone. With enthusiasm and happiness, the participants ran across the finish line, and Maja Kvehaugen Draganovic described the experience as both exhausting and fun.

description: Romerike Running Carousel is a running series with 8 different races spread across Romerike. Running is for everyone and is a social and enjoyable activity. You can choose whether you want to walk, jog, or run, with or without timing. You can register for the entire running series or sign up for individual races. Prize for everyone who completes 4 out of 8 races!

Participants can earn points throughout the series.
Prizes are awarded to those who complete a certain number of races.

description: VOM Dogrun is once again coming to Østmarka and organizing a real dog party outside Rustadsaga sports lodge. Join us for a social and fun outing with your dog, in the company of other dog lovers. You can choose to participate with or without timing, and there is a participant medal for everyone. name: Holavatnet Rundt 16
description: The Summer Carousel Holavatnet Round was first organized in 1983 and is now in its 41st season. On average, about 130 people show up every Wednesday to exercise or test their fitness in the scenic course that goes around Holavatnet. The course is 3.1 km long and consists of asphalt and gravel paths, and it is easy to take a stroller along for the round.

description: The Åsane Running Carousel is an exciting race series taking place in Bergen, Norway, from January to October 2024. Participants can choose between distances of 5 km and 10 km, with the starting gun at 19:00 for the 10 km and 19:05 for the 5 km. Race numbers will be distributed on race day from 18:00 to 18:45, and carousel participants will be assigned green race numbers that are valid for the entire season.

name: Bryneløpet
description: This year's Bryneløp takes place on Saturday, September 13, during the Potato Festival (September 12-14). The race is organized for children in elementary school (grades 1-7) and has been held since 2013. Participants start in groups for grades 1-2, grades 3-4, and grades 5-7 for both girls and boys. The course starts between M44 and Brynesenteret and goes around the lower part of Fritz Røed Park, in scenic surroundings.
course_highlights: The Bryne Race is a popular event that takes place in picturesque surroundings.
Participants can look forward to a varied and exciting course that takes them through both forests and open landscapes.
The race has several distances to choose from, making it accessible for both beginners and experienced runners.

name: Stoltzekleiven Opp
description: Stoltzekleiven Opp is a race that has been part of the running calendar since 1979. The event takes place in Bergen and is known for being a challenging uphill climb. Participants get to experience a spectacular course that takes them up the steep Stoltzekleiven, a historic staircase with 722 steps. The race has a strong focus on community and includes both individual participants and groups, and it is organized every year in September by the sports club Varegg.
course_highlights: Stoltzekleiven Opp is reportedly the world's largest uphill race, with about 6,300 participants in recent years.
The race has an elevation gain of 301.44 meters and goes over approximately 800 steps.
The event spans two days, starting on Friday and Saturday of the last weekend in September from 9:15 AM to 6:15 PM each day.

name: Hodlekve Rundt Fjelløp
description: Join the ultimate mountain race in Hodlekve, featuring races of 21, 10, and 6 km in beautiful terrain. This is an activity day for both young and old, with partners like Rab and Intersport contributing with activities and great offers. The race starts and finishes at Dalalåven, with the starting gun for the 21 km at 10:00 and for the 10 km and 6 km at 10:30. The junior race and treasure hunt will begin after 10:30, and Dalalåven will have an open café with food and drink service.

The secretariat is open in Dalalåven from 9:00 AM, and it is allowed to go out on the course to cheer for the runners.

description: CrazyRace is fun for the whole family, and the race is suitable for adults and children from 4 years old, regardless of experience or fitness level. You can run or walk at your own pace, and there are many fun and challenging obstacles along the way. Crazy Race Skedsmo is returning this fall, so bring the whole family and jump around on all our obstacles!

name: Fýri Trail by Salomon
description: Fýri Trail By Salomon is happy to invite you to the final of the Salomon Golden Trail Nordic Series. Experience the magic of Scandinavia's finest trails with two distances: 29 km and 18 km. This race will test your trail skills and provide you with an incredible experience as you run along the mountain trails of Hemsedal, where you will discover technical paths, steep ascents, and untouched wilderness.
course_highlights: Two stages, the same superhero feeling at the finish line!
Discover everything from technical trails to steep hills and untouched wilderness.
Run along the shores of some beautiful lakes and explore some of the best trails Norway has to offer.

name: Flyplassmila
description: The Airport Mile 2025 will be held on Saturday, September 20, 2025, and is known for having the "world's fastest course" on the runway of Stord Airport, Sørstokken. The course is almost completely flat and has a straight direction, providing optimal conditions for setting personal records. Participants can choose between the distances of 5 kilometers and 10 kilometers, with certified and officially measured courses.
course_highlights: The course layout is on the runway at Stord Airport, with turns resembling an indoor athletics track, 11m radius/22m diameter.
One lap is 2.5 kilometers, and the course shows a total elevation gain of 7 meters on Strava.
Race numbers can be picked up at the terminal at the airport from 10:00 AM, so please be there in good time!

name: Trail Monkey
description:
Unleash your inner TrailMonkey! 

Are you ready to play through nature like a true TrailMonkey? Monkeytrail is not like other races – it’s a celebration of freedom, movement, and playfulness. Here, it’s not just about kilometers and seconds, but about muddy shoes, grins under fir trees, and the feeling of being wildly alive.

Your adventure awaits...

Choose between two epic courses:

    6KM Trail – perfect for those who want to challenge themselves in hilly, playful terrain.

    12KM Tough Monkey Edition – for those who can’t get enough of hills, slopes, and forest magic.

    18KM MonKey Banan – for those who want to go all in: more running, more mud, more madness. And maybe a banana at the finish line.

Run, climb, laugh – and become part of something bigger...

MonkeyTrail is made for both everyday heroes and wilderness veterans. Here we celebrate movement in nature – whether you leap over roots like a ninja monkey or take your time while inhaling forest air like a Zen monk on caffeine.

You don’t need top speed; you need a sense of adventure. And maybe a little balance.

Nature's superpowers (and why you become magical by participating)

    You get a better mood just by tying your shoelaces.

    The trees give you a free mental reboot.

    Every hill you conquer grants you +10 self-respect and +5 smiles.

    And mud? Well, it’s nature’s beauty treatment for the soul.

Medal for EVERYONE – Because you are a true TrailMonkey

Everyone who finishes receives the legendary TrailMonkey medal – proof that you master the terrain and dare to play. The winners are rewarded with honor, glory, and prizes – but everyone is rewarded with nature’s applause and a solid sense of achievement.

Join us!

Become part of the pack. Run and laugh. 
Monkeytrail – it’s not just a race. 
It’s the freedom in a pair of trail shoes.
course_highlights: Our events are made for everyone - from 5 km beginners to ultra marathon warriors - and are designed with inclusivity and boundary-breaking ideas in mind.
Navigate our well-marked trails safely with support from our experienced team, and feel the energy from our close-knit, supportive running community.
At the finish line, you celebrate your achievements not only with a medal but with a warm welcome from the community, and yes, some good old tea and cake!

name: Hauernløpet
description: The Hauernløpet is a trail race of 19 km that mostly takes place on paths, with sections of gravel, through beautiful areas in Drammensmarka. The first five kilometers have an approximately 50/50 distribution between paths and gravel, while the next segment is almost exclusively on paths until 15 km. From 15 to 17 km, there is more gravel than path, before it returns to paths for the final stretch to the finish line. In total, there is about 75% path and 25% gravel.

name: Fædrelandsvennen Stafetten
description: The FVN Relay 2025 is organized by the Agder Corporate Sports Association in collaboration with Fædrelandsvennen. There will be competitions in mixed, women's, and men's categories, focusing on the joy of running, community, and team building. Each category consists of three legs, with each leg being approximately 2.2 km. The event will take place on Saturday, September 20, in Tresse, Kristiansand, and there will also be a separate active category for the fittest women and men participating in the mass start.

name: Stjernemila
description: The Stjernemila is a running event that starts in the center of Flekkefjord, right in the middle of the festivities! The course is approximately 10 kilometers long and follows a star-shaped route from the finish area, with six "arms" that take you to iconic locations in the center. The course is well-marked, and participants can have their leg times recorded on the big screen, providing the audience with a good overview. The event includes both the main race and a relay, as well as free children's races for the age groups 3-7 years and 8-12 years.
course_highlights: The runners take off in a star shape from the finish area, heading out into the 6 "arms" of the star, each of which is an iconic location in the center of Flekkefjord.

name: Oppdalsløpet
description: The traditional Oppdal Race kicks off on Saturday, September 21 at 1:00 PM! The Oppdal Race is a 3.5 km long trail run, along gravel roads and paths, with the start and finish at the NOIL square. There is an opportunity to both run and walk, and the race is suitable for all ages. Pre-registration is possible until midnight on September 20, while late registration takes place on Saturday, September 21 between 12:00 and 12:30 at NOIL. Registration is free, and a trophy will be awarded to the fastest woman and man. Welcome!

name: Kristiansand Backyard Ultra
description: The laps start every full hour, and your pace determines how long your break is before the next start. Although the ultimate goal is to reach 80.4 km, you are warmly welcome to run as many laps as you wish – or can manage. For us at Backyard Norway, running is not about showing off or the pursuit of being the best, but about overcoming oneself and pushing new boundaries. Regardless of whether this boundary is at 10, 25, or 80 km, all runners are welcome, and the last participant to finish has performed just as strongly as the first.
course_highlights: The laps start every hour on the hour, and your pace determines how long of a break you get before the next start.

name: Kongeløpet
description: The King’s Race is a recreational run that goes from Byrknesøy to Skjerjehamn. The race covers a distance of 13 km, over bridges and islands, on asphalt in beautiful coastal scenery. Just hilly enough to be challenging.

name: Skeikampen Opp

name: Driv Karusell Løp
description: The Driv Carousel (cross-country running) concludes with the final race on FRIDAY, September 7th at Drivplassen. The last race is also the club championship for all members of Driv IL aged 10 and above, as well as an awards ceremony. The Driv Carousel starts with the first race on Friday, April 22nd, with additional race dates on Fridays: April 29th, September 22nd, and September 9th. The price for all 4 races is 200 NOK.
course_highlights: The last race is the club championship for all members of Driv IL aged 10 and up, as well as an awards ceremony.
The Drive Carousel starts with the first race on Friday, April 22nd.
The price for all 4 races is 200 NOK.

name: Gjesdalmilå
description: Gjesdalmilå is a race that takes place in Ålgård and offers distances of 5 km, 10 km, and a children's race of 650 meters. The 10 km race starts between Gjesdal IL's athletics stadium and Ålgård Football Club's training field, taking participants through beautiful surroundings along Edlandsvatnet. The 5 km course has been adapted for 2024, with fewer hills and a more runnable terrain.
course_highlights: The race first crosses Åfaret and then follows down Åfaret and Solåsveien towards E39.
The 10 km race takes place around Edlandsvatnet and finishes on the track at the finish line.
The 5 km course starts on the track and has been modified to be more accessible for all participants.

name: Fagerheikongen
description: Fagerheikongen will be held on Sunday, September 21, from Lyngmyr Stadium. The race committee welcomes everyone to a real challenge in the forests around Tvedestrand! This popular race is being organized for the 47th time, and this year there is an opportunity for revenge after Lucia's comeback, who competed closely with the guys. The best local runner in Fagerheikongen will be celebrated for an outstanding course record.
course_highlights: The race is being held for the 47th time.
Lucia made a comeback at Fagerheikongen and competed with the guys.
The best local runner will be celebrated for an outstanding course record.

name: Schjongstesten
description: On Sunday, September 22 at 12 PM, the Schjongtest is being held for the 8th time, with the motto for the day: "It's okay to have fun!" Last year, 311 people participated, and the event includes two children's races of 600 m and 1700 m, as well as a competitive class/recreational run with or without timing at 1700 m. The course is marked with signs every 100 m, and at 11:45 AM, Andy will start his fun and energetic warm-up, suitable for everyone. Bring family, friends, neighbors, and colleagues for a shared experience in beautiful Schjongslunden.
course_highlights: The Schjong test offers many beautiful unconventional and traditional prizes that can entice both the eyes and the stomach.
The 1700 m course is marked with signs every 100 m.
At 11:45, Andy will start his fun and energetic warm-up, suitable for everyone.

name: Bergen 5000 Challenge
description: Bergen 5000 Challenge takes place on Sunday, September 22, 2024, starting at 5:00 PM at Fana Stadium. Challenge yourself, friends, family, colleagues, or teams to the fastest 5000m race of the fall in Bergen, consisting of 12.5 laps without inclines. The race offers recreational and elite classes, with pacers to support the participants. Admission is free for the audience, so bring everyone you know and cheer on the runners to create a great atmosphere.
course_highlights: The successful first edition of the Bergen 5000 challenge was held with a 5000m race for both recreational runners and elites, as well as a 1000m children's race.
A total of 116 participants were registered, and Gneist provided pacers in all heats to help the runners achieve good times.
The race is open to both experienced runners and beginners, providing a great opportunity to experience the community of running enthusiasts.

name: Slitusprinten
description: The Slitusprint, organized by Slitu IF Skigruppe, invites runners and recreational athletes aged 11 and up to a fast-paced 10 km road race in Slitu on Sunday, September 28, 2025, as well as a trial Norwegian Championship on 5 km. The course is officially measured by NFIF and is record-fast, featuring only asphalt as the surface and flat terrain, making it easy to run. The start and finish are at Slitu Stadium, and parking will be at Morenen Shopping Center. Timing and registration will be handled through EQ-Timing, with race number pickup on race day from 10 AM to 12:30 PM.
course_highlights: The course is officially measured by NFIF and is record fast!
With only asphalt as the surface and flat terrain, the course is easy to run and straightforward.
There were strong times and personal bests in the very fast 10 km course, despite the wind conditions.

description: We welcome joggers and runners from 9 years old to the new race series Voss Race Series 6 in 2026. The races take place on Mondays starting at 7 PM, on the following dates: April 13, May 4, June 1, June 22, August 3, and September 21. The course is 5 km, starting and finishing at the sports field, then a lap in Prestegardsmoen, continuing along the waterfront promenade and back to the sports field.
course_highlights: The course is 5 km, with the start and finish at the sports field.
The run takes place on Mondays starting at 7 PM.
The event is open to joggers and runners from 9 years old.

description: Welcome to the season's second race in the City Marathon Perseløp 2023! The date is May 24th, and the distance is 5 km. As always, the start/finish is at Marineholmen by VilVite, and the mass start is precisely at 6:00 PM. We offer a certified course, pace setters, and prizes for winners and raffle prizes from Löplabbet. Bring your friends, colleagues, family members, or good training buddies and join the race!

There will be an exciting course in scenic surroundings, perfect for both experienced runners and beginners. Asker Ski Club is pleased to invite you to this race, which starts at 6:00 PM in Asker Park.
course_highlights: The event invites both experienced runners and beginners to participate.

name: Ringshaugløpet
description: RINGSHAUGLØPET is a low-threshold race where you can test your fitness or just get a good workout. The race is organized 2-4 times a year and is open to everyone. The loop at Vallø is run counterclockwise, and the course is on asphalt the entire way. It is open to traffic, and timing is done with a personal watch. Participants report their completion or time.
course_highlights: The race is held 2-4 times a year, and it is open to everyone.
The lap at Vallø is run counterclockwise, and the course is on asphalt all the way.
Participants report completed runs or times.

name: Vom Dogrun - Kristiansand
description: The wait is over! VOM Dogrun is returning to Kristiansand and hosting a real dog party at Tresse outside Christiansholm Fortress. Join us for a social and fun outing with your dog, in the company of other dog lovers. You can choose to participate with or without timing, and there will be a participation medal for everyone. Welcome to the whole family – both two-legged and four-legged!
course_highlights: Everyone receives a medal and participant prize, including a beautiful Vom dog bowl and a race number.
VOM PUPPY WALK is a special activity for puppies – which is free to sign up for.
The competition class allows only one dog and one person per bib number with timing, while in the Open class, multiple dogs per person are permitted.

name: RUNFEST
description: Get ready for Runfest Norway – the world's most ambitious three-day street running festival. The event takes place from October 1 to 3, 2026, in Sandnes – the hometown of Olympic champion Jakob Ingebrigtsen – and offers a unique combination of elite competition and the joy of running in fantastic surroundings here on the edge of Norway. RUNFEST aims to be a unique, global event that inspires joy in running, better health, diversity, and community.
course_highlights: The event offers a unique combination of elite competition and the joy of running in fantastic surroundings.
The goal of RUNFEST is to place Sandnes and the region clearly on the map, both nationally and internationally.
RUNFEST embraces Team Ingebrigtsen's desire to inspire better health and community.

name: Ogndal KM Terrengløp Lang
description: Ogndal KM Cross Country Long is an exciting cross country race taking place in beautiful Ogndal. Participants will compete over a distance of 6 km, where Jørgen Wekre recently won gold in the G 18-19 age category. Additionally, Mosvik IL swept the board with four gold medals, including Marit Anita Karlsen as the best female runner. The race offers a great opportunity to experience nature while competing.
course_highlights: Jørgen Wekre won gold in the G 18-19 age group at Saturday's district championship in cross-country running, long course.
Mosvik IL had 4 participants in the KM cross-country running event in Vålen, Ogndal last weekend, and they swept the board.
Marit Anita Karlsen was the best female runner at the championship.

name: Stavanger Backyard
description: Backyard Stavanger is a backyard ultra that takes place in late September each year. It follows the classic backyard formula where all participants run laps of 6.7 km every hour, and you must be ready for a new lap before the next one starts in order to continue. A maximum of 12 laps can be run, which corresponds to 50 miles or 80 kilometers. The fastest runner on the 12th lap is considered the winner of the race, and the times before this do not matter. The course is partly gravel and partly asphalt, so it is important to dress appropriately and be prepared for changing weather conditions.
course_highlights: Participants run laps of 6.7 km every hour.
A maximum of 12 laps are run, which corresponds to 50 miles or 80 kilometers.
There are facilities where you can store food, drinks, changes of clothes, and extra shoes between laps.

name: Grep Grenlandsløpet
description: Join the Grep Grenland Race on August 31, 2024. This diverse race in the woods and fields is for both young and old, athletes and casual runners. Bring your friends, colleagues, and family to the race celebration at Vestsiden School in Porsgrunn, where you can experience achievement, joy in activity, and a great sense of community. Choose between distances of 5 km, 8 km, 13 km, 22 km, and 47 km, as well as a free children's race and entertainment.
course_highlights: Grep Grenlandsløpet is a diverse race in the woods and fields - for young and old - recreational runners and active participants.
The event is for all ages, and together with Eidanger IL, it includes everything from children's races to ultramarathons.
Experience the beautiful trails of nature and be cheered on by each other and all our wonderful volunteers.

name: Dølisjøen Rundt Løp
description: Slåstad Sports Club welcomes everyone to Dølisjøen Rundt 2025, which is the 48th time the race is being held. Oppstad Sports Club is a co-organizer of the race, while Odal SK is a co-organizer for the cycling segments. The race offers various categories, including a fitness class for running, cycling, or riding, as well as competitive races with timing over 12 km. Dølisjøen Rundt is known for its beautiful nature, but also for the challenging sections towards the end of the race.
course_highlights: The cycling classes include the club championship for Odal Cycling Club, featuring a tour class for cyclists over 20 km and youth categories.
The recreational class can choose between a short route of approximately 4 km or a longer recreational route around the lake of 12 km.
Running includes active classes with timing for 12 km, a youth race of approximately 4 km, and a relay with 7 legs covering 10 km.

The course is certified and nationally approved by a certified course measurer. The race takes place on Saturday, September 26, 2026, and offers distances of 5 km and 10 km.

Start and finish in Randaberg Center.
The course is officially measured and nationally approved by a certified course measurer.

name: Birken Gateløp
description: Birken is expanding its portfolio with a brand new event: a full-fledged street race in beautiful Lillehammer! This street race, taking place on September 27, 2025, will go through the center of Lillehammer with the start and finish at Lilletorget. It is an accessible opportunity for everyone, whether you are a recreational runner, an experienced athlete, or just want to challenge yourself. The event offers a unique chance to experience the city's streets, set a training goal, and build community, while a portion of the profits will go back to the local community.
course_highlights: The course will go through downtown Lillehammer, with the start and finish at Lilletorget.
Distances: 10 km (160 meters of elevation), 5 km, and 300 m (children's race).
There will be entertainment, cultural performances, "afterrun," and great deals in stores and restaurants.

description: Join us and run in Norway's fastest half marathon course! The maximum time for the half marathon is 2:30 hours due to train crossings. There will be pacers for finish times ranging from 1:10 to 2:15. All participants will receive a finisher medal, and there are cash prizes sponsored by Grue Sparebank for the top three places in both the women's and men's categories, as well as a prize for the course record.

This is the fifth year, and extra attention will be given to runners who have participated all five years. New this year is a prize of 5000 NOK for the course record, with the current record for men at 1 hour 13 minutes 49 seconds and for women at 1 hour 24 minutes 16 seconds. The race starts at 11:00 from Bjoa stadium, and the course is certified and measured by a certified course measurer. Medal to all finishers.

description: Gaular 3000 is a race that takes place around Sande, starting at the Spar store, heading towards the stadium and Døskeland Marine. The course goes over the bridge and back past the church, finishing at the bus stop. The loop is officially measured at 3 km and starts at 3:30 PM, open to everyone aged 11 and older. description: The athletics group invites you to Hydro Rundt on Saturday, September 14. The recreational class starts at 12 PM, while active runners begin at 1 PM. Both races have their start and finish at the square in Øvre Årdal, with an entry fee of 100 NOK for the recreational class and 200 NOK for the active class.

Start and finish at the square in Øvre Årdal.

name: Årefjorden Rundt
description: Årefjorden Rundt will be held on Saturday, September 28, starting from Rygge Youth School at 1 PM. The race features distances of 13 km and 8.3 km and is part of the Mossekarusellen, which includes several other races. The terrain for Årefjorden Rundt is primarily off-road and gravel, with some asphalt. The best way to view the race map is on a PC, as there are issues with mobile devices and tablets.
course_highlights: Årefjorden Rundt is part of the Mossekarusellen, which consists of 4 races: the Albyløpet at 3 km, the Ekholtløpet at approximately 7 km, the Kambomila at approximately 10 km, and Årefjorden Rundt at 13 km.
The race takes place in both Moss and Rygge, and the terrain is mainly trail/gravel, but with some asphalt around Årefjorden.
There is a mass start for the participants, which provides an exciting and social experience.

name: Gaia Backyard Hafjell
description: Gaia Backyard Hafjell is a scenic and hilly course that starts from the sports store at Gaia, goes out on Nysætervegen, and then into the ski trail towards Pellestova. The course climbs towards the weather radar located 1080 meters above sea level, goes around the radar, and continues to the cairn at Hafjelltoppen. The race is 6.7 km long, and the start is every full hour – you must return before the hour is up to continue. In 2024, there were nearly 30 runners who started on lap 12 and thus ran a total of 80 km.
course_highlights: The course goes around the radar and then towards the cairn at Hafjelltoppen.
The race takes place on a scenic, hilly course of 6.7 km featuring grass, gravel, and trails.

name: Nattland Backyard Ultra
description: Nattland Backyard Ultra is a challenging ultramarathon where participants run a lap of 6.7 km (6706 meters) within an hour, with new laps starting at the top of every hour. The race continues until there is only one participant left who completes a lap. Although the ultimate goal is to reach 80.4 km, everyone is welcome to run as many laps as they wish – or can handle. In 2026, the race will take place at Nordre Nattlandsfjellet in Bergen, Hordaland.
course_highlights: Backyard running is a loop of 6.7 km that is run up to twelve times.
The laps start every hour on the hour, and your pace determines how long of a break you get before the next start.
Participants can run as many laps as they wish, with one participant needing to finish in order to win.

description: Lierløpet is one of Norway's fastest courses, and the race takes place on a wide pathway that is well-used by runners and joggers in the Drammen area. With a distance of 10 km, this race offers a great opportunity for both experienced runners and beginners to test their skills.
course_highlights: Lierløpet is one of Norway's fastest courses.
The race takes place on a wide pathway.
The race is well-utilized by runners and recreational athletes in the Drammen area.

name: Ørsjødilten
description: We warmly welcome everyone to this year's "ØRSJØ-DILT". The race takes place at Prestebakke and has been organized for 40 years, attracting participants of all ages. The participants run the first 2.5 km together with the 8 and 21 km routes, around the football field and the lit trail, before continuing on gravel and finishing with 1.5 km in terrain. There is a lot of beautiful nature along Ørsjøen, and it is a fantastic opportunity for both locals and visitors to take part in an inclusive and enjoyable event.
course_highlights: The runners start with a lap around the football field and then 1.9 km of hilly terrain in the lighted trail.
There is an elevation gain of 60 m at the end of the 5.5 km gravel section.
Drinks and bananas are available at 6, 12, and 15 km.

name: Loddefjordløpet
description: The Loddefjord Race is an annual event that takes place in Bergen, Hordaland, and has been organized by Loddefjord IL Athletics for over 40 years. This year's race event will be held on Sunday, September 22, starting at 10:00 in Alvøen Sports Park. The race offers a varied and scenic route suitable for both beginners and experienced runners, with distances of 5 km, 2 km, and a free children's race of 400 m for grades 1-4. We aim to create an inclusive low-threshold running festival that inspires physical activity for children and families throughout western Bergen.
course_highlights: The Loddefjord Race has been held for over 40 years and offers a scenic route through beautiful areas in Loddefjord.
The children's race of 400m for grades 1-4 is completely free to participate in, and all children receive a medal for their effort.
The event has distances of 5 km and 2 km, making it accessible for both experienced runners and beginners.

name: Borredalsløpet
description: Borredalsløpet is a 10 km race that takes place on gravel roads and some on mountain trails in Fredrikstadmarka. The first race was held in 1988, and since then the courses have remained the same, although the names of the races and the locations for the start and finish have varied. In 2014, the first race that went in the opposite direction was organized. The best man ran it in 21:40, while the best woman completed the 5.6-kilometer stretch in 29:41.
course_highlights: The first race was held in 1988.
The courses have been the same, but the names of the races and the locations for the start and finish have varied.

description: Oslo Trail Challenge is a trail ultramarathon in the forest areas of Nordmarka, Lillomarka, and Romeriksåsen north of Oslo city center. Welcome to the Oslo Trail Challenge from September 27-29, 2024. The trails are unmarked, and you are responsible for navigating to stay on course, either by using GPS tracks or paper maps. Participants can choose between distances of 200 km, 100 km, and 55 km.
course_highlights: The trails are not marked, and you are responsible for navigating to stay on course, either by using a GPS track or a paper map.
Oslo Trail Challenge takes place in the beautiful forest areas of Nordmarka, Lillomarka, and Romeriksåsen.
Participants can choose between distances of 200 km, 100 km, and 55 km.

name: Tekna Veldedighetsløp
description:
The charity run is being organized for the second year in a row and will take place on September 28th. This year, just like last year, we want to highlight the importance of students' mental health. Mental health is a topic that never goes out of date, and we must continue to work on it so that we can constantly improve our ability to tackle the challenges that everyday life presents to us.

We want to support and shed light on the services provided by Mental Helse Ungdom with the funds we manage to raise. The registration fee paid upon signing up goes entirely to Mental Helse Ungdom.

Although we are running to benefit students' mental health, we want to invite adults of all ages to join in and run. The course will be set around the large Lungegårdsvann – a distance that is manageable regardless of fitness level. Participants can choose whether they want to run, walk, or contribute as cheerleaders.

Join us and use your legs for a good cause!
course_highlights: The charity run brings together students and other fitness enthusiasts for a race to support Mental Health Youth.
The event emphasizes the importance of students' mental health.
Join a meaningful running experience in the beautiful surroundings around Store Lungegårdsvann.

The race starts at 2:00 PM with a children's race for the youngest, followed by the 2.5 km at 2:30 PM and a mass start for the 5 km and 10 km at 3:00 PM. Participants receive a medal upon finishing, and there are prizes for category winners and the best runners in each distance. All distances start and finish in Revetal town center, and parking is free.

name: Øygardskarusellen 6
description: Welcome to the race carousel taking place in beautiful Øygarden. The race is suitable for children and adults of all ages, where you can be active together, be social, win cool prizes, and have fun. The races will take place over 6 Mondays, with three races in the spring and three in the fall. In 2025, a total of 6 race carousels will be held, starting at 7:00 PM, and the 900-meter race will start at 6:30 PM for children born in 2017 and later.

description: Hønefoss 5 km is an easy and fast course, officially measured by Kondis in June 2018, where many participants achieve personal records. The route mostly runs along the picturesque Storelva, with its highest point in Søndre Park, where runners are greeted by lively music from Hallingby School Band. The course consists of approximately 3 km of trail/gravel road and 2 km of asphalt, making it ideal for both beginners and experienced runners.

name: Sjusjøløpet
description: On Saturday, August 9th, the Sjusjøløpet will take place from the Sjusjøen Cross-Country Arena, and many cross-country skiers are expected at the starting line. This race, which is being held for the second time after a successful debut in 2013, offers two distances: Sollifjellet Rundt at 21.5 kilometers and Sjusjøvannet Rundt at 10.5 kilometers. The courses traverse scenic areas such as Sollifjell, Mostefjell, and Snørrvillen, with the start and finish at the Sjusjøen Cross-Country Arena. The organizing committee wishes everyone good luck and hopes for high participation.

name: Hanatrappene Opp
description: Hanatrappene Up is a mountain race taking place on Sunday, October 27th at 12:00 in Sandnes. The race ascends the 306 steps to Hanafjedle, which is likely Northern Europe's longest outdoor staircase and a popular training destination. The staircase was completed in 1955 and connects the old Hana school with the sports facility. Sandnes Idrettslag is proud to invite you to this unique race in the historic stairs.
course_highlights: The race goes up 306 steps straight up to Hanafjedle.
The stairs are a popular target for training sessions and are defined as a school route.
The record for the race, set by Torbjørn Fjeld eleven years ago, is 0:52.8 and still stands.

name: Nesbyen Backyard
description:
Nesbyen Backyard 6- and 12-Hour  
Detailed info at runnershei.com  

Date and location: October 4, Nesbyen, Hallingdal. Start at Nesbyen Sports Hall at 10:00 AM.

name: Bèrghem Ultra Marathon
description: Bèrghem Ultra Trail is our classic trail running event, offering a range of trail running distances, all set against the stunning backdrop of Hedmarksvidda. This area is home to some of Norway's untouched forests and a well-known witch mountain. Runners can expect a mix of marked trails and marked/unmarked gravel roads, but the real challenge lies in the bogs and wetlands that dominate the entire region. Don't be fooled by the low profile - this terrain is some of the toughest in Norway.
course_highlights: Hedmarksvidda is home to some of Norway's untouched forests, as well as a famous witch mountain.
Runners can find a mix of marked trails and marked/unmarked gravel roads.

The race has a total distance of 21 km and an elevation gain of 1050 meters, with the highest point at 1455 meters above sea level. This event is part of the Mountain Festival at Tyin Filefjell, where there will also be an exciting program with activities and experiences for both young and old. The mountains are at their most beautiful at this time of year, so bring your friends and family for a weekend filled with nature experiences, play, and fun.
course_highlights: The extreme distance takes place in majestic surroundings with a route over the mountains Skørsnøse, Støgonøse, and Børrenøse.

name: Hamar Backyard Ultra 50M
description: Hamar Backyard Ultra 50M is a running competition organized according to the "Backyard" principle, originating from Big's Backyard Ultra in Tennessee, USA. The course is 6706 meters long and must be completed once every hour; anyone who fails to meet the deadline for the next start is out. The competition has a maximum duration of 12 hours, allowing for a maximum distance of 80467 meters, equivalent to nearly two marathons. The winner is determined by the fastest time on the last lap if multiple participants finish.
course_highlights: The course is 6706 meters long, and it is necessary to complete one lap every hour in order to continue in the competition.

Ålesund Winter Carousel consists of 5 races held during the winter months, featuring varied distances; the main course is 10 km, while the 5 km distance turns around halfway. The races are tailored for both beginners and experienced runners, providing a great opportunity to stay active throughout the winter.

name: Vom Dogrun - Drammen
description: VOM DOGRUN is for everyone who wants to participate in a pleasant activity with their dog. You can choose to compete with or without timing, and it is a social event for both dogs and their owners. Distances include 7.8 km for the competitive class (2 laps, with timing) and 3.9 km for the open class (without timing). There is also a free VOM PUPPY WALK available, and all participants receive a dog bowl, a sample treat, and a medal, as well as the chance to win great prizes after the race.

name: Djupadalten
description: Djupadalten is an annual race organized by Haugesund Idrettslag. The race has become an important part of the sports community and attracts both local and visiting participants. With a distance of 9.3 km, participants can look forward to a varied course that takes them through beautiful natural areas, featuring both challenging sections and stunning views. Race numbers can be picked up on the 2nd floor of DeepOcean Arena on Friday, October 18, and on Saturday, the distribution will move to a tent at the Athletics Stadium.

name: Moaløpet
description: The Moaløpet is a trail run set in beautiful autumn surroundings in Bokemoa, Stokke. This year's race is expanding with a Mix class in the relay, and otherwise, we continue the traditional race as before. Welcome!

name: Hytteplanmila
description: Hytteplanmila is a 10 km road race held at Svensrudmoen in Hole municipality on Saturday, October 18, 2025. This annual street race, first organized in 2004 by IL Holeværingen, is known for its fast course. In 2019, Jakob Ingebrigtsen set a new Norwegian record for the 10 km road race with a time of 27:54. The race attracts participants from all over the country and offers a professional experience with live results and awards for both elite runners and recreational participants.

The race is considered to be set on an easy-to-run course.

name: Ekeberg Dogrun
description: The Vom Dogrun is for everyone who wants to take part in a pleasant activity with their dog. Participants can choose to compete with or without timing, and everyone is welcome to run or walk. In the competitive class, there is only one dog and one person per bib number with timing, while two dogs per person are allowed in the open class. This is a social activity for the whole family, perfect for those who want to walk, jog, or run with their dog.

name: Neskollen Ultra
description: Neskollen Frontyard is a unique Ultra race organized by Hvam IL Athletics, taking place on a relatively flat 3 km loop. Runners must complete the first lap within 30 minutes, with time requirements becoming stricter for each subsequent lap. This event is designed for the whole family, featuring a special competition for families where we crown the "Ultra Family" based on the number of completed laps. Participants who finish the first lap receive a medal, and rankings are determined by the number of completed laps within the time limit.

name: Borredalsmila
description: Borredalsmila is an exciting race that offers varied terrain and challenging hills. The courses stretch through beautiful nature in Fredrikstadmarka, and participants get to experience both challenges and natural beauty. It is designed for both beginners and experienced runners, with distances suitable for everyone. The race has been organized since 1988, and in 2014 it became the first race to run in the opposite direction.
course_highlights: The courses stretch through beautiful nature, and participants get to experience both challenges and natural wonders.
It is designed for both beginners and experienced runners, with distances that suit everyone.
The 10 km races take place on gravel roads, and partly on mountains, in Fredrikstadmarka.

name: Bygdøymila
description: Bygdøymila is a fantastic race that takes you around the entire Bygdøy peninsula in Oslo, consisting of 50 percent asphalt and 50 percent gravel on a gently undulating course. The race was first held in the 1980s before it was discontinued, but it has been revived and organized in the last couple of years. This year, there were nearly 1500 registered participants, spread across the distances of 10 km, 6 km, 3 km, and the mini race, with the most participants in the main distance of 10 km.
course_highlights: The race takes you around the entire Bygdøy peninsula in Oslo, with a course that consists of 50 percent asphalt and 50 percent gravel.
Bygdøymila has experienced a significant resurgence and has become a very popular race in recent years.

name: UM/NM Terrengløp, lang løype
description: We welcome you to the Norwegian Championships in cross-country running long course at Nordbytjernet, Jessheim! The course is planned as a loop of 1.5 km that will be run several times depending on the distance. There will also be an opportunity to participate in the recreational class, where you can add a loop up Grønlivegen for a total distance of 8 km. Remember that the deadline for regular registration ends at midnight on October 3rd.
course_highlights: The course follows a developed gravel path around the idyllic Igltjønna in Rindal Center.
It will be a 1.5 km loop that will be run several times depending on the distance.

name: Snøkuten Nordhagarunden
description: The Snøkuten Nordhagarunden takes place on October 17, 2023, and has a distance of 9.5 km. The race is part of the Snøkuten series and offers participants the opportunity to challenge themselves in beautiful surroundings. The Nordhagarunden is quite demanding, and participants experience a varied course with both uphill and downhill sections. This race is a great opportunity for both experienced runners and beginners to test their limits.
course_highlights: The race is part of the Snøkuten series and gives participants the opportunity to challenge themselves in beautiful surroundings.
The Nordhagarunden is 9.5 kilometers long and quite challenging, with varied obstacles along the course.
Only 24 raced the Nordhagarunden for time, but there were plenty of joggers with reflectors along the course.

name: Hjerteløpet 5K
description: The Heart Run 5K was held on Thursday, October 24, in Holmenkollen by the pharmaceutical company Boehringer Ingelheim, to benefit Adults with Congenital Heart Defects (VMH) and the Organ Donation Foundation. Nearly 300 people participated in the event, where they could choose to walk or run 3 or 5 km in Norway's ski arena at the top of Oslo. This was the first time the race was held in Holmenkollen, and the course was steep.
course_highlights: Participants could choose to walk or run 3 or 5 km in Norway's ski arena at the top of Oslo.
The Heart Race 5K is a refreshing fun run that starts and finishes at the Ski Arena in Holmenkollen.

The course is 19 km and mainly runs on trails and through forests, starting and finishing at Bærum Golf Club. There is also a separate 3 km race for children, and the 19 km distance caters to all levels of ambition. Each year, a few dozen runners complete more than 2 laps.

name: Kvalheimmila - Bislett
description: Kvalheimmila is a track race where everyone is welcome to participate. The race is held at Bislett Stadium, providing you with a great opportunity for a personal best in the 5 km or 10 km. The waves are divided according to desired finish times, and all waves receive pacers to help guide you to the finish line. But remember, you still have to run!
course_highlights: Kvalheimmila is Oslo's flattest and most even fun run!
The race takes place at Bislett Stadium, also known as the world record track in international athletics.
The arena is set up with a screen for passing times, upbeat music, and drink stations to ensure a great environment for fast races.

name: Bergen Maraton
description: The Bergen City Marathon offers several distances for participants, including the Sport 1 Marathon (42 km), Jæger Half Marathon (21 km), BT Relay, Oris Dental 5 km, and Vestkanten Children's Race (2 km). The course is designed to be inclusive and suitable for various skill levels, with an elevation profile that provides a diverse experience for the runners. Race day starts with a group warm-up at 7:15 AM and concludes with Bryggen reopening to traffic at 4 PM. Bergen is the marathon city number 1 in Norway.

name: Lillomarka Rundt
description: Lillomarka Rundt is a 50-kilometer loop on trails in Lillomarka, featuring 2500 meters of elevation gain and technical trails with a bit of gravel. The route passes through Sinober, which is the northernmost point, and participants are advised to bring their own food due to the length. The start is at Skytta kindergarten, and the race takes you through rolling terrain, with beautiful views from heights of 400 meters above sea level.

name: Hinnaløpet
description: The Hinnaløpet is an annual running competition held for the 39th time in Stavanger, Rogaland. There are two course options: Hinnaløpet, a challenging loop course of 9.3 km starting from Hinna Stadium into Sørmarka, where 70% of the route is on gravel and the rest on asphalt, and "Hinnaberget 5980," a shorter and less demanding variant of 5.98 km. The courses provide participants with a unique experience of the region's beautiful natural areas, featuring stage climbs up the hills in Sørmarka.

"Hinnaberget 5980" is a shorter and less demanding variant of the Hinnaløpet, with the same start and finish.

name: Checkpoint Melshei
description: Checkpoint Melshei is a low-threshold trail run that stands out because there is no fixed route. Participants must visit three checkpoints in Melsheia, but they choose their own path between them. You can opt to run on fast surfaces like gravel or asphalt, but that means a longer distance, or you can aim for a shorter route with rougher terrain off the trails. The race is held simultaneously with Hardhausens, creating a great atmosphere and a "full house" at the SI cabin on this day, complete with a kiosk, announcer, changing rooms, and lots of people.

Checkpoint Melshei is a low-threshold trail run in Melsheia in Sandnes. The start and finish are at the SI cabin.

Mærraskallen 15 km is a challenging course (approximately 15.7 km) where the first two-thirds involve a lot of elevation gain with running on trails and in marshland, while the last third is mostly downhill and on gravel roads. It is recommended that the youngest participants run together with an adult. Mærraskallen 4.2 km is a loop on the illuminated trail at Fossum, and Mærraskallen Mini 1.5 km is a race for the youngest with an open class for everyone under 12 years old, without timing.

The race takes place in Jessheim with a mass start, and the course is 3,146 meters long and flat. Simple logistics make the race efficient, with the option to take the train or park 300 meters from the start. There are also many experienced pacers to help participants find the right pace, as well as a great children's race and distances ranging from 3 km to half marathon.

The Glesvær Race is a collaboration between Glesnes Youth and Sports Club, Sotra Øygarden Hiking Club, and the Trading Town of Glesvær, and the race is sponsored by local businesses.

name: Svalandsgubben
description: Svalandsgubben Skauløp has become a term among both elite runners and recreational athletes. Every year since its inception in 1974, the last Sunday in October is the day everyone talks about. When the traditional event kicks off with a bang on Sunday, October 31, 2021, it will be for the 48th time, still in the prime of life for those enduring tough challenges. The race covers 27 kilometers of mud, marsh, and hardship, and despite the challenges, 973 participants lined up at the starting line.
course_highlights: Svalandsgubben has become a popular event among both elite runners and recreational runners since 1974.

name: Nightrun Trondheim
description: Nightrun Trondheim is an exciting running experience that takes you through scenic surroundings. The first 2 kilometers around the lake are relatively flat, while for about 1.5 kilometers, it gradually rises towards the end of Baklidammen. After that, it descends towards the finish line for the last 1.5 kilometers. The terrain is mostly gravel paths, but there are also sections with forest trails and forest floor. The route starts at the playground in the woods, across the road from Ferista parking, and you run counterclockwise.

RunRudskogen is a unique opportunity to run in the footsteps of motorsport, surrounded by the vibrant energy of Norway's most famous racetrack. Here, you can test your limits whether you are an experienced runner looking for a race event you have never experienced before, or looking for a fun activity for friends or the work crew!
course_highlights: The race takes place at Rudskogen's main track, known for its perfect asphalt.

The race starts and finishes at Frøyland School, taking participants through the beautiful and hilly landscape of Hålandsheia. The route goes around the entire Hålandsheia, offering fantastic views of the town and the sea, and includes a trip down to Buøya.

The terrain offers open nature with pine forests, deciduous forests, and spruce forests, as well as historical sites like "The Scout Cabin."

name: Åstveit 3000
description: Åstveit 3000 is a classic 3000m race taking place on November 13, 2025, with a registration deadline of November 10. The event is open to men and women aged 18 to 99, and there are limited spots in the heats. Participants are encouraged to provide their personal best time to ensure even heats, and pacers will be available. Race numbers can be picked up on race day from 5:00 PM at the athletics track.
